Lords of the Fallen 2 will now launch in April 2027, and we'll find out exactly when next month.

Recent findings suggest that the news came via a short post on X from CI Games founder and CEO Marek Tyminski. "Lords of the Fallen II: April 2027," he wrote. "Exact date in December.".

That means the Soulslike sequel has slipped again. Back in June, CI Games pushed Lords of the Fallen 2 into a Q1 2027 release window, saying the extra time would let the team refine the game and keep it clear of "a highly competitive holiday period". That was a delay in itself, as when CI Games and Epic ended the game's PC exclusivity deal in May, it was still targeting a 2026 release.

It has been revealed that last month, CI Games secured a €28.6 million (around $32 million) loan to complete production and release Lords of the Fallen 2, as well as refinance its existing bank debt, according to a stock exchange filing. The loan matures on 31st August 2027, and, as reported at the time, CI Games will self-publish the game and expects to repay the loan through its sales.

According to recent reports, lords of the Fallen II: April 2027. Exact date in December. pic.twitter.com/yYaevDqaxe.

Lords of the Fallen 2 is coming to PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store.

Sources indicate that following its announcement in 2025 and a look at gameplay during that year's The Game Awards, Lords of the Fallen 2 - which is technically the series' third game if we don't ignore the fact it was rebooted - had been steadily marching towards an unspecified 2026 launch. On PC, the plan was for it to be an Epic Games Store exclusive, but that's no longer happening after we learned CI Games - developer and sole owner of the IP - is now free from the multi-year exclusivity deal with Epic Games.

It has been revealed that the sequel has also been at the centre of heated conversations following CI Games founder and CEO Marek Tyminski's comments regarding "political correctness" and "real player feedback". The studio also raised eyebrows recently by announcing more revealing armour sets for female characters in Lords of the Fallen 2, for instance, compared to its previous project.

Eurogamer gave the rebooted Lords of the Fallen two stars, calling it "a perfectly acceptable Soulslike that's often fun to play and offers the same satisfaction at overcoming adversity", but one let down by "Soulslike clichés and performance woes".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip married in 1947, going on to make history by achieving the longest marriage of any British sovereign couple.
  • November 2, 1947: Queen Elizabeth—then Princess Elizabeth—with Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, King George VI and Queen Elizabeth (right) and members of the immediate and extended Royal Family at Buckingham Palace after their wedding.
  • The Queen and Prince Philip’s love story began back in 1939.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip married in 1947, going on to make history by achieving the longest marriage of any British sovereign couple. Back then they were, of course, Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip of Greece and Denmark, tying the knot in the rather austere years of post-war Britain. So, what really happened on their wedding day?

November 2, 1947: Queen Elizabeth—then Princess Elizabeth—with Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, King George VI and Queen Elizabeth (right) and members of the immediate and extended Royal Family at Buckingham Palace after their wedding.

The Queen and Prince Philip’s love story began back in 1939. Princess Elizabeth was just 13 years old; her dashing distant cousin, Prince Philip of Greece and Denmark, was five years her senior and about to join the Royal Navy. They met as she toured the Royal Naval College at Dartmouth; he was the young officer assigned to escort her around that day.

Determined to marry for love, Elizabeth was said to be rather taken with Philip, who was described at the time as ‘handsome as any film star.’ The pair were soon writing letters to each other, and later, occasional chaperoned meetings took place.

The couple on their engagement, 1947.

Recent findings suggest that in 1946 Philip proposed in Scotland, and she immediately remarked yes. However, her father, King George, reportedly insisted the couple resist announcing their engagement until the Princess, who was just 20, was a little older. In the end, her parents gave in to her wishes, and Philip officially proposed to Princess Elizabeth in 1947, with a three-carat diamond ring he designed using stones taken from a family tiara that belonged to his mother, Princess Alice of Battenberg. It was created by London jeweller Philip Antrobus Ltd.

Princess Elizabeth with Philip Mountbatten on their wedding day.

The Royal Family were adamant that the wedding of Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip would reflect the country’s post-war situation while also offering a chance for the nation to celebrate.

In a recent development, like many brides at the time, Princess Elizabeth had to save her rationing coupons to buy the materials for her dress but was given an extra 200 from the government to help. While well-wishers generously sent their own to the royal, they had to be sent back as rules dictated that coupons could not be shared outside of households.

Designed by Norman Hartnell, Princess Elizabeth’s wedding dress was made from ivory silk, duchesse satin and silver thread; the dress featured crystals, 10,000 seed pearls, a fitted bodice, heart-shaped neckline, long sleeves and a 15-foot train. It was made in just seven weeks by 350 skilled women since the wedding took place only four months after the couple’s engagement announcement. Norman Hartnell also designed Elizabeth’s going-away outfit.

Princess Elizabeth’s wedding day tiara was called the Queen Mary Fringe Tiara. It had belonged to her grandmother, Queen Mary, and had been given to her as a wedding present in 1893. It was remade from a tiara/necklace that Queen Victoria had bought from Collingwood and Co.

It has been revealed that as Elizabeth was getting ready on the morning of the wedding, it snapped. Luckily, royal jeweler Garrard was apparently on hand to fix it, and the Queen later revealed, “I think he taped up the spring.”.

Princess Elizabeth’s other wedding day jewelry included two pearl necklaces. The shorter of the two necklaces was the “Queen Anne” necklace, stated to have belonged to Anne, the last Stuart Queen. The other was known as the “Queen Caroline,” and is said to have belonged to the wife of King George II. Both necklaces were left to the Crown by Queen Victoria and were given to Elizabeth as a wedding present by her father.

All royal bridal bouquets contain myrtle from a myrtle bush planted by Queen Victoria at Osborne House. Princess Elizabeth’s also had white orchids and was laid on the grave of the Unknown Warrior at Westminster Abbey the day after the wedding.

There were eight bridesmaids at Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip’s wedding: Princess Margaret, Princess Alexandra, Lady Pamela Mountbatten, Diana Bowes-Lyon, Lady Elizabeth Lambart, Margaret Elphinstone, Lady Caroline Montagu-Douglas-Scott, and Lady Mary Cambridge.

Her two pages were Prince William of Gloucester and Prince Michael of Kent, both aged five at the time.

The bridesmaids were given silver Art Deco-style compacts with the couple's initials and a crown engraved on the lid, set with five cabochon sapphires.

The Duke of Edinburgh's best man was David Mountbatten, the Marquess of Milford Haven.

Knowing that Elizabeth hated cigarettes, Prince Philip reportedly gave up smoking on the morning of his wedding “suddenly and apparently without difficulty,” according to his valet, John Dean.

According to recent reports, the wedding took place at Westminster Abbey on November, 20th, 1947 at 11:30 a.m. Princess Elizabeth was the 10th member of the Royal Family to be married at Westminster Abbey.

Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip walking down the aisle of Westminster Abbey, followed by their bridesmaids and pages.

In a recent development, there were 2,000 guests in attendance, including the likes of the King of Iraq, Princess Juliana and Prince Bernhard of the Netherlands and the Hereditary Grand Duke of Luxembourg and Princess Elisabeth of Luxembourg. The ceremony was broadcast on the radio to millions of listeners.

Together with her father, Princess Elizabeth left Buckingham Palace in the Irish State Coach. (In her later years, it had been Queen Victoria’s state carriage of choice, as she declined to use the Gold State Coach following the death of Prince Albert.).

The wedding ceremony was officiated by the Archbishop of Canterbury, Geoffrey Fisher, and the Archbishop of York, Cyril Garbett.

The organist and Master of the Choristers at the Abbey, Australian William Neil McKie, was the director of music for the wedding and there were 91 singers; the abbey choir was joined by the choirs of the Chapel Royal and St George's Chapel in Windsor.

The service started with a specially composed fanfare by Arnold Bax and finished with Felix Mendelssohn's “Wedding March,” with ceremony hymns including “Praise, my Soul, the King of Heaven” and “The Lord's my Shepherd.”.

The bride and groom knelt on orange boxes covered in pink silk at the altar as a nod to post-war austerity.

On the day of the wedding, Philip was given the title of Duke of Edinburgh by his father-in-law, King George VI. After the Queen ascended the throne in 1953, she made the decision in 1957 to make Philip a prince of the UK, in addition to his dukedom.

The wedding rings were made from a nugget of Welsh gold which came from the Clogau St David's mine, near Dolgellau.

According to Royal biographer Ingrid Seward, who wrote Prince Philip: Revealed, Philip had a secret message inscribed inside his wife's wedding band, a message that only the engraver, Queen Elizabeth, and her husband knew the contents of.

After the service, a wedding breakfast was held in the Ball-Supper Room at Buckingham Palace for 150 guests only, with Filet de Sole Mountbatten, Perdreau en Casserole and Bombe Glacée Princess Elizabeth on the menu.

During the breakfast, the string band of the Grenadier Guards played music while guests were greeted with individual posies of myrtle and white Balmoral on their place settings as the wedding favors.

The couple waving from the balcony of Buckingham Palace.

Famously, the newlyweds went onto the balcony at Buckingham Palace to wave to the huge crowds on the Mall.

Although the royal couple received 11 wedding cakes, the official traditional fruit cake was baked by McVitie and Price and was four tiers and nine feet high. The wedding cake was decorated with both coats of arms, including the monograms of the bride and groom, sugar-iced figures of their favorite activities, and regimental and naval badges.

Mr Schur, chief confectioner at McVitie and Price, putting the final touches to the wedding cake.

The newlyweds cut the cake using the Duke's Mountbatten sword, which was a wedding present from the King.

According to recent reports, over 10,000 people sent telegrams congratulating Elizabeth and Philip, and around 2,500 wedding presents were sent from around the world. These included a cloth from Mahatma Gandhi that he’d woven himself, which Queen Mary mistook for an “indelicate” loincloth.

After their wedding breakfast, Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip headed to Waterloo station, joined by Elizabeth’s corgi, Susan, catching a train to Hampshire to spend their wedding night in Broadlands, the home of Philip's uncle, Earl Mountbatten.

The rest of their royal honeymoon was spent at Birkhall on the Balmoral Estate in Scotland.

Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip being showered with rose petals as they leave Buckingham Palace, London, for their honeymoon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A 17-year-old girl who had been missing for more than a year was rescued and returned home by the FBI after a friend she made while playing Among Us, and his mother, were able to track down her location and pass it along to law enforcement.

In a recent development, landon Tresp told the BBC that he and the anonymous girl "kind of just clicked" when they started chatting online while playing Among Us. She eventually told Tresp she was a runaway who'd been held against her will for more than a year. After learning more, Tresp, 16, told his mother, Khristina, about the exchange; she was initially suspicious, but after speaking with the girl directly on Discord and reading reports of her disappearance, she took action, asking for a piece of mail or document with a full name on it, which the girl provided.

According to recent reports, with that, Khristina began digging into tax and property records to find relevant addresses, which she then used to find photos on real estate sites. She demonstrated the photos to the missing girl on Discord, who picked out the one where she was being held; with that information in hand, Khristina contacted the girl's mother on social media and spoke to her briefly on the telephone, and also received a call from the FBI asking if she could confirm that the girl was still alive.

"I noted: 'I have; I video chatted with her, I've seen her'," Khristina told the BBC. "And she goes 'Oh my God, I cannot believe any of this'.".

The kidnapped girl contacted Khristina the following morning, after her alleged captor, 39-year-old Adam Hunter Harmel, had left the house. In a conversation monitored by the FBI, she noted she'd met Harmel on social media, where he'd pretended to be disabled and offered to pay her to help him get from Utah to Oregon. When he picked her up, however, he threw her phone into a river, then drove her to Oregon.

The girl told Khristina that she was kept in his basement and forced to sleep against the wall in his bed, while he kept a knife under his pillow to prevent escape. He gave her a mobile phone that wasn't able to make calls but could connect to wifi, which is how she was able to play online and eventually reach out for help.

It has been revealed that while Harmel was out, law enforcement began monitoring his street and house; when the moment came, police had Khristina tell the victim that it was time to make her escape. She was able to leave the house safely and into the custody of state troopers, while Harmel was subsequently arrested and charged with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity.

A social media post by the Salt Lake City FBI confirmed the outcome, although the crucial role played by Landon and Khristina Tresp was omitted: It notes only that "the FBI and the Rich County Sheriff’s Office have been actively investigating this case for more than a year and pursuing every lead received from across the US and in other countries.".

A separate Department of Justice press release, however, acknowledges that "on Nov. 1, the FBI received a tip about the possible location of the minor victim and that the victim met Harmel on a social media application in May 2025.".

Recent findings suggest that khristina and Landon have remained in daily contact with the girl they helped rescue, and they're trying to arrange an in-person meetup as well. "Sometimes we just sit on video chat, just so she knows she has someone that cares," Khristina stated. "She was on video last night when I cooked dinner …it's nice to know that when she has a bad day or a bad moment, she can call me right away or call Landon right away. She's doing great for what she's gone through.".

Tech Report: Six Things You Should Do Now to Optimize Your Setup for GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1146 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, you’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI.
  • Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 is absurdly large.
  • In a recent development, alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, you’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI. You’ve preloaded the game on your console, you’ve taken the next month off work, and you’ve locked your phone in a Faraday cage and set it adrift at sea. You’re prepared to lock in, and you haven’t forgotten a thing…right? Well, just to make sure, here are the most important tips to optimize your setup before you fire up the most anticipated game of the decade.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 is absurdly large. According to Rockstar, you’ll need up to 212GB of storage space. For high-end consoles like the PS5 Pro, that’s more than 10% of the available storage space, and close to half the space on the more budget-conscious Xbox Series S. There’s a good chance you’ll have to delete something to make room.

In a recent development, alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it). External SSDs are probably the cheapest route, though you’ll want to make sure to use a high-speed USB cable to connect it. It’s even worth shopping around for alternate models of SSD. For example, at the time of writing, the popular 2TB WD_BLACK external drive was close to $200, but the exact same drive in pink was $132.

You can also directly upgrade the storage of your console with expansion drives. The Xbox Series X|S supports proprietary expansion cards, while the PS5 and PS5 Pro can accept most M.2 internal SSDs. These will generally be faster, since they plug directly into the console via higher-speed connections than a drive hooked up via USB.

Industry observers note that let’s face it: Half the fun of any sandbox game is the weird, unique stuff that happens to only you. So you’re probably going to be hitting that “record recent gameplay” button more often than usual. While you’re cleaning up your storage space (or adding more), make sure to account for all the video clips you might want to save.

File size of video clips depends on a lot of factors, but 4K recordings can generally take up to 0.5GB per minute of footage. You can cut that down by saving footage in 1080p instead, but either way you’ll want to leave a little extra space.

Game footage is also a pretty good place to look if you need to make room on your console and don’t want to delete any games. Be honest with yourself: You don’t need all those clips from Horizon Forbidden West you saved four years ago. Dive into the settings on your console and find the biggest media files you forgot you even had on there.

It has been revealed that according to Rockstar, GTA 6 will be targeting 30fps across consoles at launch, which is pretty low as modern AAA games go. Part of the reason for that is all the processing power going to rendering a complex environment, but it also means you won’t need a fancy high frame rate TV or monitor any time soon to get the most out of it. Still, it couldn’t hurt to check a few settings on your display.

First, make sure you’re using a higher refresh rate than 30Hz. While the game is targeting 30fps, it is technically capable of more, so if your console can keep up, you don’t want to accidentally bottleneck your frames. This setting will vary by device, so check the manual that came with your screen.

Also, make sure you have HDR enabled on your hardware. There’s a good chance this is already turned on for your TV, but sometimes other devices can switch display modes if they only support SDR. The game will help you calibrate your HDR settings for GTA 6 specifically when you launch it, but only if it detects HDR compatibility in the first place.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re planning to buy a console specifically for GTA 6, this might be one of those rare instances where a PS5 Pro really is worth the upgrade. According to Rockstar, certain features like ray-traced shadows will only be available on the Pro version of Sony’s console.

According to recent reports, more importantly, the PS5 Pro version supports PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (or PSSR), which upscales lower-resolution images to get better detail and higher frame rates out of the same hardware. Given that GTA 6 is already starting at a meager target of 30fps on most consoles, anything that can give your frame rate a boost is probably going to feel like a welcome improvement over the baseline.

Sources indicate that I’ll tell you a secret as someone who’s spent a lot of time testing different game controllers: Most of the time, you really don’t need an expensive “elite” controller. Most of the time. I don’t buy into the idea that a taller control stick is going to make you an esports athlete. It can be nice to have, but it’s not a game changer. What does matter is customizing your controls, especially for long gaming sessions.

The DualSense Edge wireless controller is a favorite of mine, mainly because of the rear paddles and adjustable triggers. The former lets you map any button to a rear lever that you can access with your fingers underneath the controller, which can often ease some of the wrist strain of awkward button combos. And the adjustable triggers let you activate the buttons with less motion, again reducing repetitive stress.

The Xbox Elite Series 2 controller has similar features for the Xbox, as well as custom caps for the D-pad. Both consoles’ versions of pro controllers are more expensive than the standard ones, but if you’re planning to game for many hours, it can be worth it to get a controller that’s more comfortable for you.

If you have an Xbox One, you don’t necessarily have to upgrade your console to play GTA 6, but you might want to take a look at your network. GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on day one, and you’ll be able to stream the game to an Xbox One console (as long as you purchase Cloud playtime as well or get some with your Game Pass subscription). This is the only way to play on a console older than the current generation, so if you don’t want to shell out for new hardware, this might be your best bet.

Sources indicate that xbox recommends a minimum of a 20Mbps connection to run cloud gaming, but more is obviously better. If you can connect your console to a wired Ethernet connection, that would be better and provide more stability. If you can’t connect a cable, then at least make sure you’re well within range of your wifi router, and try to limit any other bandwidth-hogging applications on the network while you’re playing.

In a recent development, elsewhere in the podcast, Brody discussed how he has “doubled down” on not letting his kids “off the hook with the lessons they need to learn” in recent years. He explained that he is “trying to really be a mentor” for his children.

Recent findings suggest that “My son mentioned to me the other night, he’s like, ‘Dad, sometimes we sit down at dinner, and it’s just, like, a really easy conversation to start, and all of a sudden you get really serious, Dad,’” he recalled. “And I’m like, ‘You’re right, Benny. Sometimes I do, sometimes that coach comes out in me.’”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since the beginning of the week, the James Bond frenzy has shown no signs of stopping. On November 16, fresh Bond owners Amazon MGM Studios finally revealed the name of the actor who will succeed Daniel Craig as 007: Robert Pattinson. After years of speculation and months of intense rumors, the next James Bond now has a new face. Now, the next question on everyone’s mind: Who will be the next Bond girl?

According to recent reports, the exception in thie great debate is Léa Seydoux. The actor, who seems to be everywhere this year, played Madeleine Swann in Craig's final Bond films, Spectre (2015) and No Time to Die (2021). Her magnetic performance made Madeleine an unforgettable Bond girl, especially since her character plays a decisive role in the arc of Craig’s character: at the end of No Time to Die, the famous spy sacrifices himself to save her and their daughter, Mathilde. For the first time since its creation in 1953 by British author Ian Fleming, the secret agent in Her Majesty’s service was gone.

Léa Seydoux and Daniel Craig pose as they arrive on the set of No Time To Die on September 09, 2019 in Matera, Italy.

Sources indicate that in a recent interview on Vogue's The Run-Through podcast, Seydoux was candid about how little interest she had in her successor. “I don’t really care,” she noted with a laugh. “I don’t really care, guys. How can you?”.

Industry observers note that when pressed on who Pattinson's female lead might be, Seydoux expressed mixed feelings about the British spy's latest iteration. With the purchase of the Bond IP by Amazon, “It became American," Seydoux mentioned. “But I’m sure the movie will be great because it’s directed by Denis Villeneuve, who’s a very talented director. I’m sure he will do something great.”.

The online megamart took control of the storied franchise in 2023, after which Amazon founder Jeff Bezos controversially sought feedback on the title character's casting via X. The announcement of Villeneuve as the next film's director brought things back from the brink.

Bezos, who confirmed that he was “very involved” in the film's casting process, also seems to give Seydoux pause. In an interview with Variety, she admitted “was a bit sad when I heard that it was sold (…) but now that it’s Denis, I was like, Oh, at least it’s him, so it will be cinema.”.

Denis Villeneuve, who directed Seydoux in Dune: Part Two, will release the final installment of this epic science-fiction trilogy will be on December 16. After that, he'll be free to focus on his next major project: reviving the world’s most famous secret agent. It remains to be seen who he will choose to star opposite Robert Pattinson as his female companion—but we know that despite her fondness for the director, Seydoux will not return: Just last month, the French actress told People “I really loved being on this franchise, but now it’s ... done.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fresh details have emerged about the death of ESPN broadcaster and former NFL player Tom Jackson after the sudden loss, which friends have described as a “shock.”.

Jackson was pronounced dead at 4:15 p.m. on Friday, November 20, at Christ Hospital in Cincinnati, the Hamilton County Coroner’s Office confirmed to Us on Monday, November 23. He was 75.

Recent findings suggest that an autopsy was performed on Monday, and results are still pending. Jackson’s cause of death remains undetermined.

Jackson’s former ESPN colleague Chris Berman mentioned he had spoken “at length” with Jackson on November 17, three days before his death.

“All of us are stunned,” Berman noted in a statement released by ESPN on Sunday, November 22. “I’m stunned, we’re stunned and you’re stunned. … I was fortunate to work side by side with Tom for 30 years, primarily on NFL Primetime and Sunday NFL Countdown. It was a labor of love for our whole team, both in front of the camera and behind it. We always hoped our viewers enjoyed the shows as much as we did bringing it to them every week.”.

Berman added, “Tom was so much more than an accomplished NFL analyst. There was nobody kinder, more thoughtful, more loyal or more engaging than him. And when it came to laughter, Tom’s was frequent and unmistakable. He is easily summed up by this classic old song: ‘He’s got sunshine on a cloudy day.’”.

Jackson’s former Denver Broncos teammate Bob Swenson called his death “unexpected.”.

“I talked to him every week, sometimes every day,” Swenson, 73, told the Denver Gazette’s Chris Tomasson on Sunday. “I talked to him, and he was going back and forth about getting a back operation, and then he remarked he was going to do it. Then I texted him, but I wasn’t getting a response the last couple of days.”.

It has been revealed that before his broadcasting career, Jackson was a part of the Broncos’ iconic “Orange Crush” defense, which helped lead Denver to Super Bowl appearances 1978 and 1987. Jackson played all 14 of his NFL seasons with the Broncos and was named a First-Team All-Pro in 1977 and a three-time Pro Bowler in three consecutive seasons from 1977 to 1979.

Jackson is survived by his wife, Jennifer, and his two daughters, Taylor and Morgan.

Sources indicate that black Friday is usually a great time to grab a fresh e-reader, but the ongoing RAM crisis has made that a question mark this year: Amazon recently raised the prices of all its Kindles by around $50 and refreshed the entire lineup, which means your odds of grabbing one at a significant discount are low. But you aren't totally out of luck: If you haven't noticed, micro-e-readers—I'm talking credit card-sized, with screens that measure around four inches—are all the rage in 2026, and right now, you can pick up one of them for around $55.

Sources indicate that if you too can see the appeal of carrying all of your books with you on a device so small you'll forget it's even in your pocket, it's a great time to jump in: The recently released Xteink X4 Classic is currently 38% off for Black Friday, bringing it down to $54.87, a record-low price. Meanwhile, the smaller X3 is $55.72, or 19% off. Both are available in either "mist grey" or "space black." The discounts should last through the end of Cyber Monday on Nov. 30.

Recent findings suggest that xteink is a Chinese startup that shook up the e-reading world last year with the launch of the X4, a super bare-bones device that made up for its lack of features and usability with a cheap sub-$70 price point. Since then, a huge online community of fans has formed, sharing tips on Reddit and even coming together to crowdsource an alternate operating system that fixed a lot of early problems. Xteink quickly followed up the X4 with a slate of other devices, including the 3.7-inch X3 and the X4 Pro, which adds a front light and touchscreen (at the cost of screen clarity and two physical buttons).

The X4 Classic and the X3 improve on the original X4 with quality-of-life upgrades like a larger battery, relocated page-turn buttons, a real-time clock, and a tilt-to-turn-page feature. They're also lighter and thinner than the X4, though there is a trade-off involved: They drop the USB-C charging port in favor of magnetic pogo pins that require a separate adapter (included).

It has been revealed that these upgrades also increased the cost: The X4 Classic typically retails for $89, $20 more than the discontinued X4 and only $10 less than the X4 Pro, while the X3 rolled out at $79. But right now, the X4 Classic is just under $55, or around 38% off, and the X3 is about a dollar more. Either is a great option for those who prioritize crisp, readable text above the conveniences of a built-in light or touchscreen, as those add extra layers between the inner screen and outer glass. It's also key to understand what you're getting into: These devices support only e-books without Digital Rights Management (DRM), which means you can't use it to read your existing library of Kindle books. On the plus side, there's no longer a need to worry about flashing latest firmware if you don't want to, as the native version has been totally overhauled and is now one of your best options (though the new firmware, called "Licorice," isn't available on the X3 quite yet).

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

No. If you find the product you're looking for with a major discount right now, get it. It's not likely to drop any lower, but it could always run out of stock. Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • East Asia--and particularly Japan--has been suffering a rash of cybersecurity incidents as of late, affecting everything from major banks and cellphone service providers to city governments and small businesses.

  • One recent incident involved the PC launcher for the popular gacha action shooter NIKKE: Goddess of Victory, where malicious code would install a trojan called k2f that would compromise an individual's PC, taking screenshots, logging inputs, and installing/executing programs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

East Asia--and particularly Japan--has been suffering a rash of cybersecurity incidents as of late, affecting everything from major banks and cellphone service providers to city governments and small businesses. Gaming has been one of many areas targeted: between arcade games on Sega's network going offline, 11 million Capcom IDs being compromised, and a high-schooler hacking Bandai-Namco, some major publishers have been suffering a string of embarrassments. One recent incident involved the PC launcher for the popular gacha action shooter NIKKE: Goddess of Victory, where malicious code would install a trojan called k2f that would compromise an individual's PC, taking screenshots, logging inputs, and installing/executing programs. Unfortunately for one Japanese municipality, someone's gacha habits may have lead to a much bigger incident. Iwamizawa is a city of about 75,000 located in Hokkaido, Japan's northernmost island. It's not a place that makes a lot of news, but it recently went viral on the Japanese-speaking side of social media. As reported by Automaton, the city issued a notice that an IT sub-sub-contractor handling the city's fixed asset records suffered a security breach--specifically, a k2f hijack. Observers soon surmised that the most likely source of k2f would be someone playing a certain sexy gacha game on a work PC. The subcontractor in question, IT services company GIS Hokkaido, would then confirm to Japanese tech news site ITMedia that, yes, NIKKE's compromised PC launcher was the source of the problem. When asked if an employee or subcontractor had rolled out the game on a work PC, GIS politely replied that "they would prefer not to comment." Moral of the story? While there's nothing wrong with playing a suggestive gacha game on your own time, you probably shouldn't do it on the clock, and definitely not on a company PC, lest you become internet meme fodder.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We're just a couple weeks away from Marathon's Symbiosis update, a hefty overhaul patch that's aiming to inject some juice into the shooter's live service appeal with the addition of PvE roguelite and Team Deathmatch modes, fresh weapons, and even a social hub for hanging out with fellow runners and testing guns at the firing range.

According to recent reports, and that's all great. But today, Bungie dropped a new cinematic that presents its strongest argument for why Symbiosis should have our attention: You can play as a terrifying, sports-car scarlet robot samurai with a sword arm and jet legs.

Industry observers note that while Bungie previously revealed Bishop, the latest runner shell arriving with Symbiosis, in the patch's first gameplay trailer earlier this month, the new cinematic provides a strong sense of the power fantasy it's trying to capture. By which I mean Bungie clearly wants you to feel like a nightmarish apex predator. Like a xenomorph if a xenomorph was bright red and had cool space guns.

Sources indicate that as the trailer progresses, we watch as a team of runners is steadily cut down by a Bishop shell's unflinching onslaught: First, one of its members is culled after taking one of Bishop's throwable hacking knives to the neck, which seems to disrupt the target's functions. The next is blasted out of midair while trying to zipline away to safety. The third is hounded by autopistol fire into a position where they can be conveniently pounced on from above.

It has been revealed that but the trailer's peak moment happens as the Bishop prepares to loot one of its kills and is winged by a bullet from a nearby Rook, who evidently hoped to clean up after watching the whole fight pan out. This is proven to be a mistake, because the Bishop settles into a crouch, extending a plasma-edged sword blade from between its knuckles and engaging the jet thrusters in its calves.

Industry observers note that you know that thing in samurai movies where a swordsman does a lunging slash, leaving the body of his opponent to realize that it's been cut down behind him? It's like that. But with robots and jet propulsion. Marathon's going to have iaijutsu, is what I'm saying. Something for us all to look forward to.

Marathon's Symbiosis update lands on December 8.

This is where the protagonists Jason and Lucia cement their decision to go full Bonnie and Clyde, and since this chapter unfolds at a faster pace, you'll want to keep an eye out for a few missable items, people, and missions before you hit the point of no return that leads directly into Chapter 3. Which mission ends Chapter 2 in GTA 6? Appropriately, Chapter 2 in GTA 6 ends with the mission Checking Out after you reach the Move to Vice City point on your map, as Jason and Lucia will leave their current residence behind as they embark on a new journey to Vice City. To get there, you'll need to complete the following missions: What's in the Bag? Ambulance Chaser Just Moved In Girls' Trip Moses Daily Driver Slam Dunk Breakfast Run Coffee Break Afternoon Delight Checking Out Optional missions There's also a bunch of optional missions you can engage in, in case you want to score some more gear, unlockables, and cash before your Vice City trip: Check Out McKittrick Farm Collect Chemicals for Kyle Hit Avery Pawn Hit Kingpin Bowling Impounded Vehicle Pick Up a Gun Thrillbillies Twist Wrist, Smash, Grab Veteran Hunted (Jason only) Pay your room rent as swiftly as possible One of your primary goals in Chapter 2 should be settling your debt with the motel manager Linda, as the more you delay paying her, the higher your checkout fee will be. Talk to Wyman Chatting to Wyman and helping him out with his truck will also earn you an invite for a bit of off-roading fun with two of the missions: Thrillbillies and Twist, Wrist, Smash, and Grab. Find missing people While you don't have to tackle the Gellhorn’s Missing Tourist challenge as part of GTA 6's missing people questline during Chapter 2, it is recommended that you get this out of the way early. Starting this quest from Chapter 3 will be more challenging--for spoiler-specific reasons--and you can find those people of interest by checking nearby bulletin boards, posts, and notices. Play some pool Before you rob Frankie's Delights, go shoot a few rounds of pool to check off another task in your quest to be the biggest pool shark around. Grab some collectibles Several collectibles can be found in the Chapter 2 motel, so before you say goodbye to that location for good, grab 'em and sell 'em to help you reach a 100% completion rate in the game. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that I've sat through Ryan Murphy's takes on Jeffrey Dahmer and Lizzie Borden, so I'm no stranger to true-crime dramas that seem determined to make audiences uncomfortable. But after watching the trailer for Netflix's upcoming The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey, which premieres as part of the 2026 TV schedule, I felt more uneasy than I ever did watching either of those productions. The trailer itself is surprisingly restrained, and Melissa McCarthy looks terrific as Patsy Ramsey, alongside Clive Owen as her husband, John. Nothing in the footage is particularly shocking, at least by the standards we've come to expect from the genre. Yet I finished watching it with a sinking feeling I haven't quite been able to shake.

According to recent reports, the trailer begins on Dec. 26, 1996, with McCarthy's Patsy making the frantic 911 call reporting that her daughter is missing. Police arrive at the Boulder, Colorado, house, and the family indicates them a ransom note. We know how the search ends: JonBenét is found dead in the basement. Watching actors retrace those hours, even briefly, made me uncomfortable. The sequence feels eerily familiar because so many of us have heard the details repeated for decades.

The preview then moves into the investigation and the attention that followed. Officers question what happened inside the home, reporters crowd the family, and suspicion increasingly falls on the parents. McCarthy's Patsy breaks down, insisting, "I didn't kill my baby." There's also a chilling moment when the district attorney, played by Shea Whigham, acknowledges that even the facts investigators can establish may never satisfy a public desperate for an explanation. It's a trailer built around grief and accusation, with no resolution waiting at the end.

Sources indicate that I think a lot of that comes down to remembering that JonBenét Ramsey was just 6 years old when she was murdered in 1996. Nearly 30 years later, her killing remains unsolved; nobody has been convicted, and her mother died in 2006 without ever seeing someone brought to justice for her daughter's death. In the decades since, JonBenét's murder has become the subject of countless documentaries, television specials, and endless speculation. Netflix itself released another docuseries about the case in 2024.

I understand that this latest production may be trying to examine the media circus surrounding her death, and perhaps it will handle that responsibly. But watching the trailer, I couldn't stop thinking about how much entertainment we've already made out of this little girl's murder. Hasn't JonBenét Ramsey's death made enough money for other people?

The people making this series seem aware of that problem. McCarthy has spoken about how the public fascination with the mystery overshadowed the fact that parents lost their child, and Netflix states the drama examines the consequences of the media frenzy. I appreciate that intention. Richard LaGravenese, the showrunner, is telling a story that cannot provide the ending audiences have spent years demanding. Boulder police still describe JonBenét's murder as an active investigation.

It has been revealed that maybe the full series will find a thoughtful way to reckon with all of that. I'm certainly not questioning McCarthy's performance based on the footage we've seen. I just keep thinking about the difference between watching a fictional horror story and revisiting a real child's death for entertainment. The Murder of JonBenét Ramsey premieres on Netflix Dec. 10 for everyone with a Netflix subscription. I'm not sure yet whether I'll be able to watch it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As I continue to work my way through Ocarina of Time, the same thought keeps bubbling up in my mind like an intrusive thought: I wish I was playing Skyward Sword.
  • That’s a less controversial position to take now that the game has been ported from the Wii to the Nintendo Switch, easing the frustration associated with trying to fight your enemies while navigating the Wii version’s notoriously fussy waggle physics.
  • Combat in Skyward Sword feels more like that in a soulslike, not in its difficulty, but in the way it requires a more thoughtful approach than that in most Zelda games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword.

As I continue to work my way through Ocarina of Time, the same thought keeps bubbling up in my mind like an intrusive thought: I wish I was playing Skyward Sword. Unlike my colleagues, I did not grow up with The Legend of Zelda, coming to the series much later as a professional video game reviewer. It’s from that perspective that I’ve played a lot (though not all) of the major Zelda games and I can’t help but think that Skyward Sword does not deserve the bum rap it typically gets.

That’s a less controversial position to take now that the game has been ported from the Wii to the Nintendo Switch, easing the frustration associated with trying to fight your enemies while navigating the Wii version’s notoriously fussy waggle physics. Combat on the Switch is smoother, with thumb motion taking over for flexing your entire wrist. (If you want the old-school feel, though, you can play with detached Joy-Cons too.) With that upgrade, the directional combat, via which Link can only deal damage to enemies if he hits them at the correct angle, adds a fresh dimension to what’s been typically a standard sword-and-board affair.

Combat in Skyward Sword feels more like that in a soulslike, not in its difficulty, but in the way it requires a more thoughtful approach than that in most Zelda games. In games before and since Skyward Sword, aside from specific gimmicks like reflecting an octorok’s attack back at it, you’re mostly just flailing and whaling. Skyward Sword forces you to slows you down. You cannot beat an enemy with wild, unconsidered strikes. You must observe the way it defends and break through that defense.

Skyward Sword’s exploration cannot compare to that of Wind Waker or Breath of the Wild. But I think the lack of variety in overworld exploration on your companion bird is made up for by the game’s dungeons, which are some of the series’ best and most unique. I loved shifting forward and backward in time to navigate the Lanayru Mining Facility and the Sandship, and I appreciate how here, the series’ long-present motif of time travel has been shrunk down and made into a discrete game mechanic in a way the series hadn’t really done since Majora’s Mask (another fave of mine).

But honestly, the most enduring qualities of Skyward Sword are the stories and characters. This is the game that let the Groose loose! Groose starts as a petty, meathead bully jealous that Link has Zelda’s attentions. But rather than let that embitter him which, as video game tropes go, might have involved him showing up as a late-game midbossâHi, Seifer from Final Fantasy VIIIâthe feeling empowers him to discover his own destiny, and he winds up lending Link a much-needed helping hand. (Hello again, Seifer from Final Fantasy VIII.) There have been other lovable Zelda side characters who go on their own journeys of self-discovery, but I think Skyward Sword‘s singular focus on one journeyârather than on retelling similar stories split across multiple characters like the champions in BotW, for exampleâmakes Groose stand out that much more.

I also loveÂ this version of Zelda and Linkâthe bold girl and her best friend who are both transformed by their destiny and duties but remain connected due to their sweet and enduring friendship. They are always connected, that’s what the whole series is about. But some versions of them are closer than others, having a dynamic that’s deeper than simply a princess and her knight. Wind Waker had a little bit of that definition. Skyward Sword, though, deepens the relationship between Link and Zelda more effectively.

In a recent development, there’s a beautiful scene between them in which Zelda tearfully apologizes to Link for manipulating his feelings for her to force him to become the hero their world needs. She’s a true princess, taking responsibility for the pain she’s caused Link while acknowledging it needed to be done, and accepting an eternity of slumber as punishment to keep the evil threatening their world at bay. When he rushes toward her to catch her before she seals herself away, almost to say “I don’t care about that, I care about you,” I teared up, moved by how Link was able to convey so much emotion and love for Zelda without saying anything. More than any previous version of the central pair, Skyward Sword‘s Zelda and Link feel like they’re the genesis of the pair we get in Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, arguably the series’ best versions of them.

In a recent development, skyward Sword has my whole heart, and I know that makes me rare among Zelda appreciators. But so much of what we’ve come to love about later Zelda games, narratively and mechanicallyâremember, this is the first game that let you skydive and slow your fall with a sailcloth!âyou can see Nintendo experimenting with in Skyward Sword. For that alone, it deserves your reconsideration.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that before the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping press tour began, Mckenna Grace knew she wanted to be method dressed for her appearances. Made a household term by Law Roach and Zendaya, method dressing is when actors wear looks that pay homage to the film or show they’re promoting: See Zendaya’s on-theme looks across red carpets for Dune, Spiderman, and The Odyssey for a slew of examples.

With the fresh Hunger Games film, it’s Grace’s turn to adopt the trend. A super fan of the Suzanne Collins book series and their film adaptations, Grace—who plays District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner—took a hand in the styling for her press run, weaving easter eggs into every look. Her stylist, Molly Dickson, was up for the challenge of translating Grace’s deep-cut references into custom and archival looks from Monique Lhuillier, Gucci, Celine and more.

In a wide-ranging conversation, Dickson breaks down all the looks that set the Hunger Games fans’ hearts aflame, from Rue’s blue dress to Katniss’ Mockingjay gown, and all the threads that came together for Grace’s most memorable press appearances yet.

Vanity Fair: How did you get into styling?

Molly Dickson: I went to college in Minnesota and my major was advertising. Two weeks before I graduated, I called my mom and stated, "I'm not into this. I don't wanna do advertising." She said, "Well, what do you wanna do?" I told her, "I wanna do fashion. I wanna go to Latest York." She said, "No, absolutely not.".

According to recent reports, right after I graduated, I went to LA, this was 2009 during the recession, and no one was hiring. I got an internship at Marie Claire in Newly introduced York, and enrolled back into college to get school credit to intern at Hearst. I worked at Marie Claire as a market assistant for almost two years, and then I left and assisted Leslie Fremar for seven years. That's when I fell in love with celebrity. Then ten years ago, I went off on my own.

What would you say are your aesthetic influences as a stylist?

It has been revealed that my personal style relates very similarly to Sadie Sink's style, very effortless. She always wants to be very comfortable and easy, never anything frilly or over the top. Just a simple, beautiful dress, and you let it speak for itself.

Mckenna is a massive fan of the original film series, so it’s clear you’re pulling from there as influences when dressing her. Is it a collaborative process when coming to one of these referential looks?

She's obviously a very huge fan of the franchise. We actually started having conversations about this tour in April, which is very early to start having conversations. I could just sense her excitement around it. She started sending me mood boards, and I actually looked back today at the mood board and it was, it was a lot of Katniss Everdeen. It had Joanna on it, and it was filled with these really strong female characters from the franchise.

What she really wanted to hit was Katniss’ wedding gown look and the Mockingjay look with the wings. I was really stumped on how to pull that off without making it overly costumey.

It has been revealed that mckenna kept asking, "What's going on with those?" I knew the vision, but I didn't know how to execute it. I was working with Keke Palmer and the designer Michael Ngo. He was making some cool music costumes for Keke, and I asked, "Michael, could you make this silver piece?" 'Cause I really had no idea how to get it done.

He remarked, “I don't think I can do that. You know what? Just give me a day, let me play around with it." That night, he said, "I figured it out." We got the piece and I thought, "Okay, it needs to be a wedding dress under,” so I reached out to all the bridal houses. I wanted it to be vintage because it would tell a pretty story. Monique [Lhuillier] ended up sending a ton of wedding gowns, and the day before Mckenna came in for the fitting, I actually tried the wedding dresses on myself with the silver piece.

Sources indicate that I sent Mckenna five dresses, and the one that she ended up wearing, she said, "That's it. I don't even need to try anything else. That's the one I'm gonna wear." Then, it was a matter of finding the right event to wear it to because it’s pretty nice, very dramatic.

In a recent development, she was in Paris for the Miu Miu show, and I brought it there because she had the Hunger Games Museum event. It was a whole conversation with her team, like, "Is it the right moment? Is it too much for this event?" Her PR noted, "No, this is the perfect moment. It's the best way to kick off the tour." The response with the Hunger Games fans—I have never seen anything like it before, ever.

What was the experience of having her be such a big part of the styling process?

It has been revealed that it makes my job so fun because she is so passionate about it and she loves Hunger Games so much, even just finding subtle nods back to the movie. She would say, "I wanna do a ladybug look." Thom Browne did that amazing ladybug dress, I thought, "That's so cool, but it's not really her personal aesthetic." So it’s finding ways to keep it still true to her personal style while maintaining the nods to the film.

According to recent reports, the way you seem to understand Mckenna feels something similar to the connection between Katniss and Cinna in The Hunger Games. When pulling looks for her, what comes into play? How do you make her come through and not be lost in the lore of the stories or the dress?

Mckenna had remarked that she maybe wanted to do a red or a dark pink feather look because in the books [Maysilee] gets attacked by the red birds which are like flamingos. I'm pulling in all these red feather dresses and on the runway, this one dress looked amazing. Mckenna said, “That's perfect for the flamingo reference.”.

But we put it on her and it was so massive, and she's so petite so she was just getting swarmed. I remarked, “Let"s not force it.” The goal was for her to feel comfortable in the look rather than just getting each reference.

The public has been really excited about these looks. Are you thinking about the response to the looks when you’re putting them together?

There's been some conversations in a fitting, like, "Oh, the Hunger Games fans are gonna get this." They're gonna see the inspiration, they're gonna understand it.

But I wouldn't say we're choosing a look because ‘Oh, this is gonna go viral to the Hunger Games community.’ Mckenna is a super fan herself so if she's getting excited about the look, everyone else that's a fan of the franchise is gonna get excited about the look.

Mckenna Grace in Betsey Johnson.

Do you feel any pressure to top the last outfit after each premiere?

Yes. I think it was Paris because that wedding dress did get so much press. In that fitting, it felt like, "We gotta keep our game up high." It's been really fun for my team and market assistants because a lot of the girls that work with me are huge fans of the movie. They're not even seeing it as work. They're like, "Oh my God, this is so exciting. Look at this. This looks like this from the movie.".

Sources indicate that what was the inspiration to do method dressing for this press run? What do you think is the value?

Mckenna knew back in April, she said, "I wanna do method for this." I personally did not read the books. I'm a visual person, so I've seen all the movies. Lionsgate was able to let me go with the cast when they first saw the movie because my agent was like, "Molly needs to go to the movie to get inspired before this press tour. She can't do a method dressing press tour without seeing the movie.".

Even as the tour was going on, Mckenna kept sending me latest references and quotes from the book and stuff like that.

Recent findings suggest that what made you take it to the next level? From paying homage to not only characters, but the actual actors from the films like Jennifer Lawrence at the 2011 Oscars to even dressing like set pieces from the film.

It has been revealed that that was all Mckenna's vision. On her first mood board, she had a lot of Jennifer Lawrence's red carpet moments because she's such a huge fan of Katniss and Jennifer Lawrence.

With the Rue reference, Mckenna thought that color was just very Hunger Games. It wasn't until she put the dress on, her mom noted, "Wait, this is Rue's dress." So that was just fate. I would love to take credit for that.

Why do you think that this styling has generated so much attention?

I think it’s when you do method dressing for such a big franchise and you really are passionate about it. The thing is that Mckenna is so excited and passionate about this movie. She has noted, “I didn't think that I would love doing fittings so much. I used to hate doing fittings.”.

Mckenna Grace in Elisabetta Franchi.

Because every look is so intentionally tied back to Hunger Games and she's such a big fan, it's literally like playing dress up with her. I think the fans see it, she's so relatable because she's a fan that all these fans think, "Wow, like, she's a fan and she got to do this." She’s the fangirl living out her dream, and the fans are excited for her that she finally gets to do this.

What do you think are the best kinds of projects to implement method dressing with/works best with? What does it work best with?

I think the major movies that already have a fan base, like Barbie or Wednesday, Being able to pull inspiration from existing books or films makes it so much easier for a stylist rather than a movie that no one's seen before. There's no curiosity or momentum about it because you're starting from scratch, whereas Hunger Games, Barbie, Wednesday, there's already a level of expectation.

Sources indicate that the looks for this press run have been a mix of archival, new, and custom pieces. How do you make that choice? How important is it for you to create an archive for Mckenna?

In a recent development, it kind of is a mix of what we’re able to source. Mckenna really wanted to pay homage to Joanna's character with that scene where she's like, "My stylist is always putting me in trees." She's like, "I wanna do a tree reference." And I'm like, "How in the world am I gonna find a fashion reference that's a tree that's not a costume?".

In a recent development, I love the challenge of sourcing the market, and so do the girls on my team. I think it was 2011 Phoebe Philo where Celine did some tree references in the collection. But just because we find it online doesn't mean that we can get it. So then it's reaching out to every vintage dealer, every rental house, asking, "Do you guys have anything like this?" And they might have it, but they're like, "It's already gone, someone has it." I ended up actually finding the Celine tree dress on the RealReal, and I bought it. I love RealReal.

It has been revealed that what is your approach to dressing different clients? For instance, you mentioned Sadie Sink earlier, can you walk me through how that process differs from Mckenna?

According to recent reports, it's very different between each girl. I let them set the pace. If they wanna be involved, great. If they just wanna show up to the fitting and not even know what's gonna be there, I try to accommodate whatever direction they wanna go. I have one client that literally last week has sent me over 200 references of dresses that she wants, and another girl that's like, “I really don't care. Whatever you tell me to wear, I'll wear it.”.

Every girl is different, and what makes my job so interesting is that it's not the same. Everyone has very different styles. I think the most notable part of a job as a stylist is to keep their style true to them and not just force my style onto them. Mckenna's way more girly, Sadie is a little bit more casual, it’s just taking their style and elevating it a little bit.

Will you do any looks inspired by Mckenna’s character Maysilee? The looks have been mostly referential to things and people from past stories. Are there influences of Maysilee in the looks that fans haven't been able to pick up on because the film wasn’t out yet?

It has been revealed that in a couple days, she’ll be in Miami for press, and she's wearing a very Maysilee inspired, purple Miu Miu dress that has a white collar. When she wears it, everyone's gonna be like, "Oh, that's Maysilee." She really wanted to have flowers and necklaces because Maysilee is really into jewelry, so it’s very light and flowery.

Can you break down the outfit for the Latest York City premiere?

Industry observers note that we are doing the Mockingjay dress, the one with the wings, and that was another thing that I was very stumped on. I'm like, "What designer's gonna make these wings?" I had this woman in LA who does wings, she's done Halloween costumes and music videos.

Mckenna Grace in Pamella Roland.

Industry observers note that in the first fitting, I pulled this navy Pamella Roland gown. The fabric is really, really cool. It's like a shimmery kind of organza. I thought, "That's the right color,” but I wanted it to be strapless. I went back to Pamella Roland and they were like, "We can make it in strapless." Mckenna was very keen on having some sort of embellishment to replicate Katniss because she had screen printing on the gown and it kind of looks like wings in a way.

Pamella then drew all these CADs with diamond wings on it, and then we got the wings made. We did the final fitting and I almost started to cry. Her mom's taking videos and it's epic. It's so exciting because the fans were doing polls on what she's gonna wear to the premiere.

It's full circle, we started with the wedding dress, Mckenna did the fire gown, and then we ended with the Mockingjay dress.

What was the hardest look to pull together?

Mckenna Grace in custom Cong Tri.

I think design-wise, it was the fire gown.

Getting the fire printed on the fabric was really hard. I had a while back done a custom Cong Tri gown for Cami Mendes for the Masters of the Universe tour. It was like a gold beaded gown, and I remember I really liked the fabrics that they used for it.

So when I was thinking of who could do this fire gown, I reached out to them first, and I'm like, "Can you guys do something that looks like a fire? Like, she's literally on fire." And they're like, "No. We don't think we can." And again, they were like, "Give us some time." They came back and remarked, "We did all these testing on the fabric." I'm like, "Yeah, you did it. You did it.".

It has been revealed that what's really funny is we were at a fitting at Mckenna's house with the fire gown in a garment bag, and one of her friends stopped by. It was just a tip of the dress showing and her friend mentioned, "Oh my God, you got a fire gown." Then I thought, "Okay, people are gonna get it.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, according to every Diablo 4 player known to man, I screwed up by skipping its last season.
  • Even though the Season of Hell's Legacy is about to come to an end, Blizzard has delivered good news for me and everyone else who missed it: Most of it will remain in the game permanently.
  • On December 1, when the Season of Tyrael's Gambit begins, all of the unique Prime Evil boss fights will still be available, along with the Diablo world boss, Moophisto, and a handful of Diablo 2-inspired items, including the Hellfire Torch Charm.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, according to every Diablo 4 player known to man, I screwed up by skipping its last season. Blizzard shoved just about every iconic Diablo 2 boss and item it could think of into the modern game, and, by all accounts, it was one of the best seasons it ever had.

Even though the Season of Hell's Legacy is about to come to an end, Blizzard has delivered good news for me and everyone else who missed it: Most of it will remain in the game permanently.

On December 1, when the Season of Tyrael's Gambit begins, all of the unique Prime Evil boss fights will still be available, along with the Diablo world boss, Moophisto, and a handful of Diablo 2-inspired items, including the Hellfire Torch Charm. However, the craftable items, like the Enigma chest piece that gives you a free teleport skill, will not carry over.

In a recent development, even without all the craftable unique items, that's quite a lot of stuff to keep around. Blizzard tends to ditch seasonal additions as soon as a new season starts, and you usually have to wait a while to see them slipped back into the game in a slightly altered form. The overwhelming excitement around the Diablo 2 content must've convinced Blizzard it was worth putting in the work to keep them around.

Industry observers note that I would've been happy if the portal to Tristram, the rickety old town at the center of Diablo 2, was all that came back. Blizzard pulled off an incredibly faithful remake of it, complete with the old guitar theme and the voice of the blacksmith Griswold. And if you follow the hidden steps to make the Hellfire Torch, you'll be able to visit Uber Tristram, a special version of the town where you can square off against all three of the series' major villains, the Prime Evils, at once.

Diablo 4 was always kind of light on hidden quests and bosses, so it's nice to see that Blizzard found a way to bring an notable part of the series back. I'll be curious to see what else comes to the game over the next three years before Diablo 5 arrives. The Amazon class will drop next year, but no expansions are planned to fill the gap. Hopefully Blizzard will take this opportunity to experiment with more things like the Diablo 2 anniversary secrets before it moves onto the sequel.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 has raised the bar for open-world games, and Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzyński is feeling it.
  • Recent findings suggest that "GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real," Sarzyński wrote online.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 has raised the bar for open-world games, and Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzyński is feeling it. Online, the developer jokingly commented about GTA 6 setting a fresh gold standard for the genre, a level of quality that makes him want to pack up his Cyberpunk 2 development bags and call it a day. "GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real," Sarzyński wrote online. Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle. Cyberpunk 2 is canceled, Imma go sweep autumn leaves in my backyard now." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OAN_BXmVR0g Don't worry, Cyberpunk fans, because Sarzyński believes the game will offer a unique "flavor" compared to GTA 6. "Seriously though, I think we're doing something of our own, with a different, unique flavor," he wrote in a follow-up post. "GTA is impressive in a way all great art is; it expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed." Meanwhile, Cyberpunk 2077 has had a great 2026, as the release of the new Cyberpunk Edgerunners anime series once again drove the game's numbers up. A meaty patch also helped draw new players, and Cyberpunk 2 game director Gabe Amatangelo recently shared more thoughts on how the sequel is evolving beyond his original vision as more people join the project. Other developers across the industry have also commented on GTA 6, and Naughty Dog world design director Michael Barclay also believes that it is a technological achievement. "I've made video games for 19 years, and GTA6 appears to me as a Bugatti Veyron would to a nervous Victorian child," he wrote. Payday 2 game director David Goldfarb has been utterly astonished by what he has seen so far, while The Last of Us: Part 2 and Star Wars: Jedi - Survivor character artist Del Walker wrote that he can't believe what he's seeing (and how some black magic might be involved): https://twitter.com/locust9/status/2123203448057536751 https://twitter.com/TheCartelDel/status/2123632078457831663 GTA 6 has had a phenomenal start, selling 44.9 million copies in its first weekend and making $4 billion. The first post-launch patch has also gone live, though we're not too sure what it does yet. For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you're shopping for an iPad this holiday season, you might be a bit intimidated by Apple's price tags.
  • This is Apple's least expensive tablet, with an MSRP of $449.
  • It has been revealed that the iPad A16 isn't Apple's best iPad (that would be the iPad Pro).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you're shopping for an iPad this holiday season, you might be a bit intimidated by Apple's price tags. The iPad mini starts at $599; the base iPad Air is $749; and the entry-level iPad Pro is a whopping $1,199. Most of Apple's iPad line certainly lives up to its expensive reputation.

That's where the iPad A16 comes in. This is Apple's least expensive tablet, with an MSRP of $449. But despite being Apple's "budget" option, the iPad A16 shouldn't be ignored by customers looking for the best all-around device. In fact, it's really the best iPad for most people, which is why I named it the best tablet gift of 2026. What's more, retailers are giving the iPad A16 a $50 discount ahead of Black Friday, bringing the entry-level price down to $399.

It has been revealed that the iPad A16 isn't Apple's best iPad (that would be the iPad Pro). It doesn't have the best display, the best camera, or the best processor. But it doesn't need those things: This iPad has a display, camera, and processor that are good enough for most use cases, without unnecessarily driving up the price. Simply put, it's one of the best tablets you can buy right now.

The iPad A16 has a large, 11-inch (technically 10.86 inches, according to Apple's fine print) IPS display with a brightness of 500 nits. As the name implies, it has Apple's A16 chip, the same processor as the iPhone 14 Pro and iPhone 15. That chip is about four years old at this point, and while that means it won't be as fast as Apple's newer SoCs, it still holds its own with iOS 27. It comes with two cameras: One 12MP wide camera on the back, with support for 4K video recording, and a 12MP Center Stage camera on the front.

Recent findings suggest that apple indicates this iPad can run for 10 hours while browsing the internet on wifi or watching video. You charge the tablet with USB-C, which supports data transfer up to USB 2.0 (which nets you 480Mb/s transfer speeds). It also comes with other perks you might expect from Apple's more "pro" tablets. You can connect the iPad to an external display, up to 4K resolution at 60Hz. It also supports two Apple Pencil models: The USB-C Apple Pencil and the first-gen Apple Pencil.

Sources indicate that the only real consideration here is storage: This model comes with 128GB of storage, which can run out fast. It's particularly usable for consumers who rely on cloud storage or mostly stream their entertainment. But if your giftee aims to store photos, videos, or music on their iPad, it's worth considering upgrading. The $50 discount applies to most storage models, as well as the cellular iPad options, except for the 512GB models: The wifi-only model has a smaller discount, while the cellular option has a $100 discount.

Sure, the iPad A16 doesn't have the fastest processor, an OLED display, support for newer accessories, or Apple's sharpest cameras. But all of the specs it does have are enough to run the things you need on iPadOS. If someone on your list is looking for an iPad for web browsing, streaming, messaging, and light gaming—and they don't need something for professional work—this device is likely more than enough iPad for them.

Justin Hartley and wife Sofia Pernas aren’t letting his success on Tracker prevent him from taking on more projects.

Industry observers note that news recently broke that Hartley, 49, and his production tech giant, ChangeUp Productions, are developing upcoming medical drama Dr. Lucia at NBC. Based on the Mexican telenovela Dra. Lucía: Un Don Extraordinario from Azteca TV, Marimar Vega will star in the titular role.

Davah Avena will serve as writer and executive producer alongside Pernas, 37, Julianna LaRosa of ChangeUp Productions and Sheree Guitar, who will also executive produce the upcoming project.

It has been revealed that according to the official synopsis, Dr. Lucia follows the titular Lucia, who is “a first-year resident at a prestigious Phoenix hospital whose life takes an unexpected turn following a near-death experience.”.

“Suddenly experiencing psychic visions, Lucia finds herself relying on extraordinary instincts that transform her approach to medicine and help her become the physician she’s always aspired to be,” the description continued. “But as her abilities intensify, she begins to fear that her visions may actually be symptoms of the same hereditary illness that drove her sister to madness.”.

Sources indicate that hartley is already in development on another upcoming TV show after Deadline reported that ABC is working on a TV adaptation of Isabella Maldonado’s novel A Forgotten Kill. Hartley will executive produce through his overall deal at 20th Television while Diana Son will write and executive produce the project alongside fellow EPs Ken Olin and Maldonado.

Recent findings suggest that A Forgotten Kill, which was released in 2024, is centered on ex-Army Ranger Dani Vega. According to the official synopsis, Dani is “a Nuyorican from the Lower East Side and dauntless FBI agent whose specialty is breaking codes and detecting patterns.”.

Sources indicate that the description continued: “As part of a task force, Dani is partnered with NYPD Detective Mark Flint. Their clashing styles give them an edge in solving crimes and expose an undeniable chemistry, but Dani is haunted by a secret: a family tragedy in her past that comes back to put her career and life at risk.”.

A Forgotten Kill is the second novel in Maldonado’s FBI Special Agent Daniela Vega series, which follows A Killer’s Game and came before A Killer’s Code.

Hartley will balance A Forgotten Kill with CBS’ hit series Tracker. Based on Jeffery Deaver‘s novel The Never Game, Tracker follows Hartley’s Colter around the country as he helps to find missing people and solve mysterious cases.

After spending three seasons filming in Vancouver, news broke in May that Tracker was awarded $48 million on $129 million in qualified expenditures, prompting its move.

Tracker is 20th Television’s biggest series to be brought back to California with the help of a tax credit. Before that, Prime Video’s Fallout moved from Upcoming York to Los Angeles, while Dan Fogelman’s upcoming NFL drama, The Land, was given a $42.8 million tax credit.

Recent findings suggest that “I’m proud of what we built in Vancouver. I’m also very excited we’re bringing Tracker to L.A.,” Hartley said in a statement at the time. “I’m looking forward to continuing to tell these stories alongside the fresh, fresh places we’ll be heading to next. Most importantly, I want to thank the fans for showing up for us every step of the way. We couldn’t do this without you.”.

Harley later broke his silence on the shakeup.

It has been revealed that “In terms of tone and character, I don’t think it’ll impact the show at all,” Hartley told The Wrap in May. “Our show is a road show. Our character goes from town to town across the United States of America and meets people from all different walks of life and helps them out. These strangers become kind of his family in a way.”.
