📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spoilers ahead for Sunrise on the Reaping.

The Hunger Games movies (which are streaming with a Hulu subscription) have been wildly popular for a decade, and fans were recently treated to another book to screen adaptation with Sunrise on the Reaping. Francis Lawerence's upcoming blockbuster featured younger versions of a number of beloved characters, with Stranger Things star Maya Hawke playing District 3 Victor Wiress. I wanted to see more of her towards the end of the movie, but the 28 year-old actress has another POV.

Sunrise on the Reaping is crushing at the box office, showing how much the public still loved being in Panem. After Haymitch wins his games, we see a shot of Wiress looking bruised after being tortured by The Capitol about Beetee's blueprint to break The Arena. I had the privilege of interviewing the cast ahead of the movie's release, where I asked Hawke if any scenes of her character ended up on the cutting room floor. She told me:.

Sources indicate that no, I remember talking to Francis about this actually, and it would be too, too disturbing. You know, I think that with these movies, there's always a line that you're trying to walk of like telling the story as written and also making sure that it is like right for audiences. And I think that Francis said it would be too disturbing. And so we don't get to see really what happens, what goes down with us.

Despite being a franchise about young people killing each other, The Hunger Games movies have all been PG-13. As such, Lawrence and tech giant have to be specific about how violent the imagery can be. While I wanted to see more of Wiress, Hawke maintains that it would have been too "disturbing" to watch the beloved Victor being tortured by President Snow's forces. She's probably not wrong, as much as I wanted to see more of her take on the character.

A post shared by CinemaBlend (@cinemablend).

Later in our same conversation, Maya Hawke explained the upside of not having to shoot these difficult scenes as Wiress. As she told me:.

I'm grateful for it because those scenes are hard to act. By hard I mean like painful. Um, but I also was sad about it because they're fun and as well, so.

Obviously Hawke would have crushed it if we saw Wiress' torture and interrogation, but that ultimately wasn't something that was ever going to be part of Sunrise on the Reaping. The movie had to cut plenty of scenes like Maysilee killing a Gamemaker, although that wasn't the case for Hawke's character.

Sources indicate that in our chat I asked the Do Revenge actress if Wiress had a mental break as a result of her torture, transforming her into the character we were introduced to by Amanda Plummer in Catching Fire. She confirmed to me:.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

It has been revealed that that's what Francis and I talked about, yeah. That's sort of like a massive break that leads to the kind of version of her that we meet later.

I've still got FOMO about not getting more of Wiress, but I understand why it didn't happen. After all, Sunrise on the Reaping is a story about Haymitch above all. There was a ton of content to stuff into the movie's 158-minute runtime, so there was only so much time to dedicate to characters like Wiress and Mags.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters now as part of the 2026 movie release list. We'll just have to wait and see if Suzanne Collins gives us more prequel novels, allowing the beloved franchise to return to the major screen in the process.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that “Cancer does change you,” Kate Middleton says, emotion clear in her voice. “It changes your body, it changes you physically. But there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.” These words come not at as an Instagram post or at a public event. Instead, they're the voice-over in a previously unannounced documentary about the Princess of Wales and her life since she disclosed a diagnosis of cancer in 2024.

According to Kensington Palace, which announced the film on Saturday, Heal is “a deeply personal new documentary from The Princess of Wales, exploring life beyond diagnosis and the many ways people find comfort, strength and hope in the face of serious illness.” It will air on the BBC in the UK on November 29, and in the US on NBCUniversal on November 30.

Recent findings suggest that heal follows Kate Middleton during her participation in one of the United Kingdom’s most demanding endurance events: The National Three Peaks Challenge, which she completed this summer. In less than 24 hours, the princess climbed the three highest mountains in Scotland, England, and Wales: Ben Nevis (4,413 feet), Scafell Pike (3,209 feet), and Yr Wyddfa–Snowdon (3,559 feet). The undertaking wasn't just a personal effort, as it was also in support of the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, an organization that supports people living with cancer before, during, and after the disease.

The documentary will also support that organization, Kensington Palace notes, saying “All funds received through the documentary's distribution have been directed to The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity to help people living with and beyond cancer.” The Royal Marsden Hospital, at which Middleton received treatment, is also referenced in the film, as Middleton's brother, James, asks her “Isn’t it when you leave the Royal Marsden, you ring the bell?”.

But while many patients participate in the bell-ringing ritual at the conclusion of treatment, Middleton claims she missed out on that moment. “Yeah, but I didn’t ring the bell,” she replies. “So maybe this is your ringing of the bell,” James responded, suggesting her Three Peaks experience was that symbolic peal.

While Prince William is no stranger to documentary work, nor are Prince Harry and wife Meghan Markle, this is Kate Middleton's first venture into the format. Perhaps to ease her into the project, Heal's Director of Photography is a face quite familiar to the Princess: Will Warr, the filmmaker behind her video announcement marking the end of her chemotherapy treatments.

According to recent reports, “Through this documentary, The Princess hopes to help others navigate diagnosis, recovery and life beyond cancer and transform access to holistic cancer care which supports wellbeing, resilience and quality of life during and after diagnosis,” Kensington Palace says of Heal, a message underscored by Middleton's words in the trailer. “You know, healing is a journey. How to reconnect with the things you once knew and how to find a sense of hope and joy alongside uncertainty.”.

In a recent development, “It’s clear we're not meant to face life’s challenges alone,” the princess claims as the trailer concludes. “Things can renew and grow. Often it is through pain that we realize that there is a greater beauty that lies beyond that.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Another awards ceremony is struggling with how to handle an influx of genAI games. The Atari Homebrew Awards is in its ninth year, or at least it was going to be. It’s been canceled after its organizer hit an impasse with how to handle submissions that might have been made with AI.

“Keeping up with the large number of AI assisted game development had become increasingly difficult as this year wore on with some developers even releasing multiple games a week with the aid of AI,” ZeroPage Homebrew wrote on the Atari Age forum (via Time Extension). “This flood of latest AI games forced me reevaluate the way games were qualified and judged for the upcoming AHAs.”.

The task for ZeroPage wasn’t simply going through all of the submissions; it was figuring out what cutoff, if any, to have for AI use. Allowing games that were 100-percent generated by AI was out of the question, but what about games that used AI for music, art, or coding? How much of the game could be made by AI before it went against the purpose of the whole awards ceremony?

According to recent reports, linked below an key announcement you should probably read. Please keep in mind this won't change the ZPH stream and we will keep playing all the awesome games made by the community!https://t.co/0odTADzfh9.

— ZeroPage Homebrew (@zeropagehomebre) November 23, 2026.

Recent findings suggest that on top of that, there are no easy ways to vet the amount of AI used to make games. It requires that people honestly disclose it, leading to a grey area in which community reactions can lead to witch hunts and testing software can lead to false positives.

Sources indicate that “We were always able to come up with a solution for small challenges in previous years but the advent of AI marked a seismic shift in the way retro games were being made,” ZeroPage wrote. “I saw no path forward and made the difficult decision to suspend the Atari Homebrew Awards this year.”.

The forum post now has hundreds of comments as consumers react to the news and debate AI’s place in the Atari homebrew scene and beyond. “Most people who use AI are tools. (derogatory),” one person wrote. Another said a “tool” was exactly what AI turned a work colleague of theirs into. “[He] told us how when he woke up in the middle of the night to go to the bathroom he would check if there was any pending question so he could unblock the AI agent,” the person wrote. “He also confessed he started to dread looking at his phone because answering would take 15-20 mins…his sleep patterns were going the way of the dodo.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that the SE 3 does just about everything you'd expect an Apple Watch to do.
  • According to recent reports, it comes in two sizes (40mm and 44mm) depending on how large or small you prefer your watch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple has three main Apple Watch "lines." There's the flagship, at the moment the Series 12, which represents Apple's mainstream wearable. For athletes and users who think they'll put their watches through some extreme scenarios, there's the Ultra line, currently the Apple Watch Ultra 4. And while both the Series 12 and Ultra 4 are excellent devices in their own right, they can be pretty pricey (particularly the Ultra). That's why the third category, the SE, is actually best for most people, and Lifehacker's choice for best smartwatch gift of the year. Better yet, the third-generation SE is currently $50 off ahead of Black Friday, perfect for most people asking for an Apple Watch this year.

Industry observers note that the SE 3 does just about everything you'd expect an Apple Watch to do. It, of course, has a heart rate sensor to keep tabs on your pulse, including high and low heart rate alerts; the ability to track dozens of different workouts and exercise types (including swimming, thanks to the device's water resistance); a sleep tracker with daily analyses available in the Health app; notification forwarding to check in on your alerts without opening your iPhone; and the ability to send and receive text messages.

According to recent reports, it comes in two sizes (40mm and 44mm) depending on how large or small you prefer your watch. No matter which model you get, the watch comes with the S10 chip, Apple's last-generation watch processor. While it isn't as fast as the current S11 chip, the S10 is more than capable of running watchOS 27. Apple states the SE 3 can run for up to 18 hours on a single charge, and up to 32 hours in Low Power Mode, with fast charging from 0% to 80% in 45 minutes.

The majority of the features missing from the SE 3 aren't essential. Apple's other watches have things like bigger, brighter displays, additional health tracking tools like hypertension alerts and an ECG sensor, longer battery life, and Audio Intelligence—the latter of which might be a benefit to miss, depending on who you are.

If your giftee wants or needs any of those additional features, Series 12 or Ultra 4 might be a better choice. But for anyone who wants the essential Apple Watch experience, the SE 3 is simply the best-value watch Apple sells right now—especially at this discount. Right now, the watch starts at $199 for the 40mm watch, or $229 for the 44mm. You can also save on the cellular versions of these watches: $249 for the cellular 40mm watch, and $279 for the cellular 44mm model.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

According to recent reports, black Friday sales officially begin Friday, Nov. 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, Nov. 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by Dec. 2, 2026.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that things are moving fast.
  • According to recent reports, what we do know for sure is that Rockstar is taking notice and has already begun cracking down on the highest-profile projects.
  • For now, the only thing to do is observe and report.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that things are moving fast. Now that an illicit Xbox build of GTA 6 is out in the wild, anonymous modders are racing to port it to PC, and the work is progressing faster than many expected. At this rate, it's possible that a static recompilation of GTA 6 will run on a PC in a matter of days. It's also possible it will take much longer to produce a playable build that's actually on par with the console versions.

According to recent reports, what we do know for sure is that Rockstar is taking notice and has already begun cracking down on the highest-profile projects. As always, downloading pirated software is illegal and can infect your PC with malware, and that last bit is doubly true in the dubious AI era we now live in.

For now, the only thing to do is observe and report. Here's where things stand with GTA 6 PC ports.

Several projects have made it as far as booting the game and using menus, and at least one has seemingly managed to move around in-game with bugged out lighting, but it's hard to verify clips making the rounds when so many are obvious fakes.

Dozens of groups of anonymous modders and vibecoders. So many, in fact, that several websites dedicated to tracking the progress of GTA 6 recomp efforts have also appeared. One of the tracker sites, Portwatch VI, has a list of projects ranked by their "playable" completion percentage—best not to take those made up figures as an accurate estimate of when a port will be complete. The top five are:.

Until very recently, the Leonida project was among those making impressive progress, but the group's creator (a 15-year-old) quit the project after Rockstar got its Discord server taken down.

Keep up to date with the most crucial stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Every GTA 6 recomp project is based on the same thing: An illicit Xbox build of GTA 6 released online by Cyberleek, the notorious leaker who previously shared video of a GTA 6 development build months before its release.

With GTA 6 being the biggest game in the world at the moment and not available on PC, there is an outsized motivation to get it running.

Recent findings suggest that A recomp refers to static recompilation, which is the result of reverse-engineering a game's code to make it run on other hardware (usually a PC). If you want to read further on how that's achieved, PCG alum Wes Fenlon's excellent Read Only Memo newsletter has what you're looking for.

Recent findings suggest that as for how GTA 6 ports (and ports for other new games) are coming together so promptly, the answer is AI. The advent of AI coding tools like Claude have greatly expedited the work required to create a static recompilation of games on another platform. What used to take months to years now takes hours to days. Recomps that heavily use AI are often buggier, messier, and have fewer features than human-made fan projects, but they are fast and functional.

It's way too early to speak in absolutes, but I'm comfortable assuming that the first "playable" recomps will require an exceptionally powerful PC.

That guess is based on GTA 6 being an obviously demanding game and also some recent precedent: The earliest Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake recomps that've appeared online have high system requirements to perform as well as it does natively on Switch 2—and, well, GTA 6 has a lot more happening under the hood than a 28-year-old Zelda game.

Industry observers note that that's the significant question. My money is on no, it won't. To switch up plans on a dime would assume that Rockstar is sitting on a polished PC version that it could put out any day, and I'm not convinced that's the case. The current rumor, preceding all of this leak business, is that the PC version of GTA 6 is planned for Q1 2027 (so anytime before April).

That's not to say Rockstar couldn't expedite the process if it wanted to—they certainly have the resources to achieve the unlikely.

Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto 6 has plenty of fun Easter eggs--many of which tie back to earlier games in the series--but you can also find a few nods to other megapopular game franchises hiding within the vast map of Leonida. If you take a detour along the north side of Lummox County, you'll come across an area in the woods that looks like it'd be right at home in a Super Mario Bros. game, and you can even collect two distinct caps for your troubles--which might suggest that the greater Mario multiverse theory is true after all. How to find the GTA 6 Super Mario Bros. Easter egg in GTA 6 You can mark this location on your map, as you can find the reference to the Nintendo mascot in Lummox County. It's up north from Mount Kalaga, at the end of a twisty road that seemingly goes nowhere: Hit the bong, dude Once you've arrived, scout the area for a purple tarp that has a bong sitting on it. Smoke it, get high, and climb the structure in front of you. You'll notice that there's a plume of smoke coming out of the one column, and if you stand in it, an invisible block will appear above your head. Smash the block Jump up, and you'll smash the block. You won't get any gold coins for your trouble, but you will get a nostalgic tune and two caps that reference Nintendo's favorite plumbers, Mario and Luigi. Collect the caps Each cap has an initial embroidered on it: "J" for Jason, "L" for Lucia. You can add them to your collection, or leave them to gather dust; it's up to you. As mentioned above, GTA 6 has references to a lot of pop culture. Someone at Rockstar Games is clearly a huge Dexter fan, Bigfoot is on the prowl, and I really wish I'd chosen the elevator without a killer clown inside it. For everything else on the biggest game of the year--and maybe even the decade--check out GameSpot's GTA 6 guides hub.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday sales officially start Friday, November 28, and run through Cyber Monday, November 30, 2026, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before it's over.

It's Cyber Monday, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before the sales are over.

Follow our live blog to stay up-to-date on the best sales we find.

Browse our editors’ picks for a curated list of our favorite sales on laptops, fitness tech, appliances, and more.

Sales are accurate at the time of publication, but prices and inventory are always subject to change.

Not every Black Friday or Cyber Monday deal is as sweet as it seems. With electronics and tech in particular, you could be buying last year's model that has actually been on sale since the summer—and was maybe a better price a few months ago. Here’s how to avoid impulse buying a misleading Black Friday “deal” and make sure you’re getting the best bang for your buck.

When you see products like food, clothes, or home goods with a big "Black Friday" or "Cyber Monday" tag slapped on them, it's probably safe to take advantage of that deal. Chances are it's the same exact product you'd find on other days of the year. The same can’t be stated for a TV, laptop, and other tech deals, where the product itself is constantly being upgraded.

According to recent reports, because tech is always evolving, and retailers want to move inventory before new models come out, electronics are especially susceptible to a practice known as "price anchoring." That's when retailers mark up prices in the weeks leading up to Black Friday, before "slashing" those prices back down, giving the appearance of a deal that isn't really a deal at all. Still, when you see that marked-up number, aka the "price anchor," you might get tricked into thinking you're saving money when you're not. There's also the false sense of urgency that gets created. It's second nature to assume that anything labeled "deal" won’t last long—even when this so-called deal price has actually been going on since the summer.

Price anchoring isn't even unique to Black Friday. The nonprofit Consumers’ Checkbook tracked prices at 25 major retailers over 33 weeks in 2022 and found that more than half the items tracked were offered at false discounts every week or almost every week. Less common, but also worth noting, is a known practice of "derivative" or retailer-exclusive models produced specifically for the holiday shopping season. These versions often feature cheaper components, fewer features, or lower specifications than their regular counterparts. A 55-inch TV from a reputable brand might look identical to the year-round model, but it could have a lower refresh rate, inferior panel technology, or fewer HDMI ports.

In the same vein, that "amazing deal" on a laptop might come with last year's processor, or a smartphone that's about to be replaced. The glitch isn't that the tech is an older model, but again, it's that it probably has been at this low a price, or lower, since the summer. Alternatively, some deeply discounted electronics are refurbished units or open-box returns that have been repackaged. Again, while this isn't necessarily a bad thing, impulse buyers may not fully realize what they're buying.

Sources indicate that the key phrasing here is impulse buying. Events like Black Friday are psychologically engineered to trigger impulse purchases. Limited-time offers, countdown clocks, and "while supplies last" warnings create artificial urgency. When you're caught up in the moment, it's easy to convince yourself you need a new tablet, smartwatch, or gaming console, even if you hadn't considered buying one before.

In a recent development, to avoid a low-key scam, do your research. The easiest way to tell that you’re getting the correct product is by checking the model or serial number. And with online shopping, finding and double-checking those numbers is quick and easy. In addition, don't just compare prices—compare specs. Look at processor speeds, RAM, storage capacity, screen resolution, refresh rates, and connectivity options. A $300 laptop isn't a deal if a slightly more expensive model offers significantly better performance that will last longer.

If you do see a deal that catches your eye, it could pay to wait. Cyber Monday, post-Christmas sales, and even January clearances often feature electronics deals that rival or beat Black Friday prices, all without the famous chaos and pressure. Then again, you risk more “out-of-stock” results if you wait, so the risk is up to you, depending on the popularity of the item you’re eyeing (and how badly you want it).

The bottom line: Don’t fall victim to a falsely advertised lower-quality product, and do a little research to find actually good deals ahead of time.

Sources indicate that yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

GTA 6: All The Secret Controls And Gameplay Features You Might Have Missed

💡 Key Takeaways
  • On the surface, Grand Theft Auto 6 has a pretty standard control scheme for its protagonists.
  • On the surface, Grand Theft Auto 6 has a pretty standard control scheme for its protagonists.
  • In a recent development, instead, you're left to discover them as you play, and each one adds another layer of immersion to the experience.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On the surface, Grand Theft Auto 6 has a pretty standard control scheme for its protagonists. You've got everything you'd expect for exploring its open-world environment, from options to sprint to aiming your gun, but there's a whole lot more to the game when you start experimenting with the inputs. Whether you're driving or jogging, Jason and Lucia are capable of a whole lot more, and these hidden features aren't thrown at you when you start the game. Instead, you're left to discover them as you play, and each one adds another layer of immersion to the experience. If you don't want to accidentally stumble on them, here's a closer look at every hidden gameplay feature we've discovered so far. For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub. Go into first-person mode Want to examine the world in more detail around you? Press L2 (LT on Xbox) to highlight something, then press R3 to go into first-person mode. Ordinarily, you can't move around in this mode, but there is a glitch to force the game to lock you into first-person. Change shoulder cameras Not too big a fan of the default over-the-shoulder aiming in GTA 6? You can switch which shoulder you aim from during combat by holding the left button on your D-pad while aiming with L2. Quick-swap between weapons At the same time, you can also quick-swap between weapons by tapping Triangle/Y while aiming, allowing you to keep blastin' like you're some sort of Frank Reynolds character. Do a combat roll! Need to close the gap rapidly and avoid taking a few lead injections? Tap X/A while aiming, and you'll do a combat roll. Do a backflip! To show off some athleticism, run towards water, and as you get to the edge, hold X/A on the controller to do a backflip. Pistol-whip when you're out of bullets Got a gun in your hand, but you're out of bullets? It turns out that firearms are still good for inflicting blunt-force trauma, as you can use the melee attack (Square on PS5, X on Xbox) to knock enemies out. Choke enemies out For a stealthy beatdown, start a fight in GTA 6, grapple your opponent with R2, and then hold Square/X to set them up for a chokehold. Press the indicated D-pad button on your controller, and you'll trigger the chokehold. Chain-jump across gaps If you're running across an area that has multiple small gaps, you can tap X to jump across and tap it again to keep your momentum going. Your car door is also a weapon Instead of damaging the hood of your car in GTA 6, put a dent in your door by smashing it into a pedestrian. Like melee attacks, you can hit Square/X on your controller while driving to nail an unlucky person with the door. Your feet are technically free when you're on a bike And if you're not in a car? You can relive your Road Rash days by hitting the melee button to kick someone instead while you scoot around on a bike. Change how you wear your cap Whether you like to wear your cap in a traditional sun-blocking style or backwards, you can swap the position of your headwear easily. Just open the items and weapon wheel by holding L1, select items, and navigate to your cap. Press X/A and you can switch styles. Distract enemies with some whistling, which I can't do in real life GTA 6 makes for a surprisingly good stealth game, and for those scenarios where you need to draw enemy attention, you can whistle at them. Crouch, take cover, hold L2 to aim at a target, and press Triangle/Y to whistle. Loiter like a champ with leaning actions One of the cooler features in GTA 6 for photography fans is the option to lean against walls and railings. When you're near a wall, you can hold Circle/B to lean against it, and when next to a railing, press L3 to rest on that structure--pretty cool for when you want to take a photograph of Jason or Lucia while they chill out. In a recent development, it's official: After more than five years together and nearly a year of engagement, Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando have tied the knot. The couple were married in the desert hot spot of Palm Springs, California on Saturday, November 21, an outdoor ceremony held at Frank Sinatra’s former mansion, with Wayne Coyne, frontman of The Flaming Lips and a Cyrus collaborator, officiating.

It has been revealed that the 33-year-old singer and the 28-year-old musician—Morando is the drummer for the band Liily—had kept their plans a secret until Friday, when TMZ broke the news. Confirmation of the impending celebration emerged that same evening, during the dinner that capped off the rehearsal, when Miley’s half-sister, Lily-Rose Purcell, posted a photo on her Instagram Stories of a menu featuring the couple’s initials. This is Cyrus’s second marriage, following her alliance with actor Liam Hemsworth from 2018 to 2019.

Sinatra’s former home in Palm Springs, where the wedding took place.

According to images published in outlets including People, the ceremony venue was decorated with white flowers and large candles, with Sinatra’s pool in the background. Miley Cyrus wore a long-sleeved white satin dress with a plunging back and no veil, while the groom opted for a classic black tuxedo with a bow tie.

Among the guests were the bride’s mother, Tish Cyrus, accompanied by her husband, actor Dominic Purcell, and Miley's sister, Noah Cyrus. Also in attendance was the singer’s father, Billy Ray Cyrus, along with his rumored fiancée, British actress Elizabeth Hurley, and her son, Damian.

Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando on February 01, 2026.

In a recent development, as the bride has recounted in past interviews, her relationship with her now-husband began in 2021 following a blind date organized by mutual friends. That same year, they went public by attending the singer’s New Year’s Eve TV special in Miami together. Their engagement came to light in December 2025, when, during another of those joint appearances, Miley Cyrus posed on the red carpet wearing a diamond ring that turned out to be her engagement ring.

Recent findings suggest that one of the most emotional moments of the ceremony took place just before the couple exchanged their vows, when—according to multiple outlets— Dolly Parton’s “Love Is Like a Butterfly” began to play. The nod follows a similar one Miley made last month, when she broke down in tears over Parton's death during a performance at the Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles.

According to recent reports, “Me and Dolly, we are eternal. Nothing in this life could ever tear us apart, and I’m gonna see her again,” Cyrus told the stadium crowd in October, per The Hollywood Reporter. “And I can’t fucking wait because I miss her,” Cyrus tearfully continued. “Some of the greatest music that we have today was written, produced, performed by my Aunt Dolly.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that you can cancel your Prime subscription via web browser by first logging into your Amazon account. Amazon has a Cancel Your Prime Membership button on its support page to launch the process, or you can follow the steps detailed on Amazon's page:.

Head to Amazon.com in your web browser.

Hover over the Accounts & Lists menu on the top-right of the window, then select the Prime Membership option.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

Note that Amazon requires a bunch of clicks to finalize your cancellation, giving you lots of “opportunities” to change your mind.

Open the Amazon Shopping app on your mobile device.

Click the three horizontal lines on the bottom right.

Under Shop by Category, select Prime.

On the top bar, slide all the way to the end and select Help.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

Recent findings suggest that as mentioned, closing your account will immediately end your access. Amazon also offers you the option to pause your benefits and billing temporarily instead of canceling them completely. Either way, your Amazon account is still active—you simply won’t have Prime benefits.

Finally, if you have other subscriptions connected to your Prime account, those will end when your billing is up. And if you signed up for Prime through the Android mobile shopping app or the Prime Video Android app, you’ll have to go through Google Subscription to manage your membership.

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto VI is a visual and audial treat, and is easily one of the most technically impressive games on the current generation of consoles. But it isn't without issues, especially if you're trying to experience the sights and sounds of Vice City with all the moody contrast and bright highlights that HDR offers. That's due to an HDR calibration tool that isn't exactly working in the way that you expect it. Like many other games, GTA VI doesn't use the system-level HDR settings on either the PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X|S. Instead it features its own calibration tool, which lets you adjust the maximum brightness, black levels, and paper white values that work best on your display. While the tool makes calibration seem straightforward, there's an issue with it that makes it very unreliable. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=d3UaVoP6dPg Specifically, the maximum brightness and paper white point values seem to be linked in a way that is both unclear and incorrect. Normally you would set these values individually, with maximum brightness set according to the value your display supports and the paper white value that looks best to you. GTA VI instead changes the maximum peak brightness value it is storing as you change the paper white point. For example, if you set a maximum peak brightness at 1000 nits (a typical value) but then reduce the paper white point (given how how its default is), the peak brightness value reduces as well, with no indication to you that it's happening. HDR enthusiasts and handy calibration assistors HDTVTest and GamingTech have both confirmed the issue, and provided some rough workarounds until Rockstar (hopefully) releases a fix. The idea is setting the maximum brightness value higher than your display supports, but in line with what the game is expecting based on the paper white point value to choose. It's confusing, but GamingTech has drawn up a table that might help depending on your display's specifications. HDTVTest's approach is similar but with different recommended values for both the ideal paper white point and black level values, so you'll need to do some experimenting on your end to find what suits your setup best. Rockstar has released the first patch for GTA VI, but it mostly addresses some widespread bugs that players have been encountering since launch. HDR issues were also common at launch with Red Dead Redemption 2 but eventually were fixed sometime after, but if you're like 45 million other people and planning to explore Leonida today, then hopefully these tweaks let you get it looking its finest.

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rockstar Games.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is a massive world filled with an incredible amount of detail and simulation. This includes the game’s dynamic and realistic weather system, a feature Rockstar hyped up quite a bit before launch. However, some players online aren’t seeing much rain and are claiming Rockstar lied. The reality is that, yes, rainstorms happen, but you might not be seeing them very often for a few reasons.

Industry observers note that if you search around Reddit or Twitter, you’ll see a lot of people complaining that it never rainsÂ in GTA 6. However, you can also find amazing clips of thunderstorms pummeling Vice City. And I can confirm that when I played GTA 6 pre-release, I saw rainstorms and other weather events, like fog.Â  So what’s going on here? Why are some people suggesting the weather system in GTA 6 isn’t working or was a lie, while others, like myself, are dealing with thunderstorms?

THIS ISN'T JUST RAIN. THIS IS ENVIRONMENTAL ARTISTRY AT AN ABSURD LEVEL! ð¤¯.

Sources indicate that just look at the rain dripping off the sides of the bridge, the incredibly atmospheric overcast skies and the way the entire scene comes together. GTA 6 genuinely looks like a work of art!

I'm quiteâ¦ pic.twitter.com/NjbjmeYHV7.

— VideoGameDetails (@VideoGameDetail) November 24, 2026.

First up is that it does seem like something was borked with GTA 6‘s dynamic weather system at launch. On Monday, the first post-launch patch for GTA 6 arrived and fixed an issue that, according to Rockstar’s patch notes, led to the weather not changing for extended periods of time. So yeah, one reason it might not have been raining in your game is because of a bug.

However, even after the patch, some people are still claiming it isn’t raining in GTA 6. And maybe something is still bugged. The more likely explanation is that people don’t realize just how dynamic and advanced the weather is in GTA 6.

In all previous Grand Theft Auto games and most other open-world games, when it rains in the game, it rains across the whole map. That’s not how weather in GTA 6 works. Instead, storms, fog, and other weather events can happen locally and in small parts of the map. At one point I was flying a plane and it was sunny, but ahead in the sky were massive dark clouds. As I reached them, I entered a rainstorm. As I left the clouds behind, the rain stopped. So it’s very possible that it is raining somewhere in your GTA 6 world; you just aren’t in the spot where the rain is falling.

I’ve also seen some people suggesting the weather is locked to certain conditions earlier in the game, which seems plausible but hasn’t been confirmed by Rockstar yet. Once I reached chapter three of the game, I had a few in-game days when it rained a lot. I started to miss the sun.

The point is that, no, Rockstar didn’t lie. Grand Theft Auto 6‘s dynamic weather system is so good that I think some people are just dodging the rain without realizing it. The size of the map and the randomness at play in the system may mean that you go for a while without encountering rainy weather, but keep playing and sooner or later, the storms will come.

Cavallari added that she feels like she has “gotten to say everything I’ve wanted to say” in the last three years of her podcast.

According to recent reports, “It’s been a really fun, wild ride. Like, when I started the podcast, I was actively dating and I was newly single, and it was really fun, all my dating stories. It’s been a journey, and I’ve been so happy to have you guys on this ride with me,” she continued.

Cavallari admitted that the downside of her podcast has been “having to be out there every single week.”.

“There would be headlines all the time about the podcast, and I don’t like that stuff,” she explained. ”But in the past, if I was in pop culture a lot, I could reel it in, right? I could go silent on socials. I could not do any interviews. I could stop doing everything. I don’t have that luxury with this podcast to be quiet when I want to be quiet.”.

Recent findings suggest that cavallari also stated she’s “really busy” these days with her kids — Camden, 14, Jaxon, 12, and Saylor, 11, whom she shares with ex-husband Jay Cutler — and her Uncommon James jewelry and beauty brand. “I don’t want to be just f***ing grinding every day,” she said, recalling a two- or three-week break she took a little over a year ago.

“If I could go back and do things differently, I probably would have asked for, like, three or four months off and then came back like guns blazing, but, you know, again, everything happens for a reason,” she added.

Industry observers note that over the weekend Nvidia released a hotfix that supposedly caught the bug, only for people to discover it merely delayed its onset. Forum people have been testing out version 621.40 and it seems to have not only stopped the Nvidia container service from freaking out and rewriting its log, but also caught a bug with custom cursors that would make them turn gray. Which is nice.

According to Bank of America stock analyst Omar Dessouky, the initial success of GTA 6 reinforces the company's belief that the game has a massive reach, and with that comes the possibility of monetizing the players even more when the next evolution of GTA Online is released.

In fact, SeekingAlpha reported that Dessouky said he is so bullish that he believes GTA Online alone "can become a multibillion-dollar franchise, potentially larger than Fortnite." He said Fortnite generates as much as $5 billion in annual revenue, and GTA Online could be bigger in the fullness of time.

According to recent reports, the stock analyst went on to raise his price target on Take-Two's stock to $350. That would represent a significant upside, considering Take-Two right now trades at around $210/share.

Take-Two's stock got hammered in 2026 and never fully recovered. The tech giant's shares are down 16% so far in 2026 and down 12% over the past year.

In a recent development, investing is a long-term game, though. Zooming out, Take-Two has crushed it since GTA 5 released. If you bought $10,000 worth of Take-Two stock on the day GTA 5 came out in 2013, and never sold, you'd have more than $120,000 today.

Recent findings suggest that as for the next iteration of GTA Online, Rockstar has not said a word about what to expect or if such a mode is even coming. GTA 6, after all, is marketed as a strictly single-player game.

According to recent reports, that being remarked, it seems plainly obvious that a new version of GTA Online is coming. According to multiple reports, the new version of GTA Online for GTA 6 could launch in 2027, along with a PC edition of the game.

GTA Online for GTA 5 has been, and continues to this day, to be a major moneymaker for Rockstar and Take-Two, and it's expected that the developer will find even more ways to make money from players with GTA 6 Online. Some have theorized that GTA 6 Online could have some form of user-generated content, for example, potentially leading to a marketplace of some kind.

GTA 6 introduced on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and it reached 32.5 million copies sold via pre-purchases alone. On day one, GTA 6 generated $3.79 billion in revenue. Over the first four days, GTA 6 has climbed to 44.9 million copies sold and more than $4 billion in revenue, according to a report.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it’s a balmy late-September day in London, and Dolly Alderton is explaining to a befuddled Emma Frost what “iPhone face” means. Frost has never heard the term; her fellow showrunners Alderton and Zoe Kazan have.

“You know [how] you look at some faces, like Rosamund Pike’s face—it looks like it’s never seen an iPhone? It looks like it’s seen a lute and a loom,” Alderton tells Frost.

“So actors who look like they’re comfortable in a period show, rather than feeling inherently modern,” claims Frost, as understanding dawns. Alderton and Kazan affirm her: “Yes, yes. Exactly.”.

Now that Frost gets it, she turns back to the group’s Zoom screen. “Sorry, what was the question?”.

Kazan began her career as an actor, while Alderton started out as a dating columnist and Frost was a sculptor and painter. Now all three are overseeing vastly different but comparable Netflix period dramas, each based on a classic work of literature: East of Eden (Kazan’s, which was released October 1), Pride and Prejudice (Alderton’s, out December 3), and The Age of Innocence (Frost’s, coming February 18). They’ve gathered in a London conference room at Netflix headquarters for a roundtable discussion about art, work, the unique experience of adapting a beloved book—and, apparently, iPhone face.

Industry observers note that though this is the first time the trio has met face to face, their conversation flows so easily and naturally that interrupting them with questions sometimes feels impolite. Early on, I note that all three of these novels are, on some level, about unconventional women. Alderton, Frost, and Kazan pause for a moment, considering this Lit 101–level observation.

“That’s true, I think,” agrees Frost.

And then they’re off to more interesting topics.

Vanity Fair: Have you read each other’s books?

Dolly Alderton: No, I haven’t read either of your books.

Alderton: Did you read them at school, or did you read them for fun?

It has been revealed that frost: Pride and Prejudice I read when I was a teenager at school. East of Eden I read first about 15 years ago, I think.

Alderton: So Em already wins the round table.

Frost: And for both of you, was it the thing you most wanted to adapt?

According to recent reports, alderton: I would never have dared to dream to. I was so overwhelmed when I was first approached. I just thought, it’s such a precious IP. It would be way too much, and I wouldn’t be the right person. But then when I was asked to pitch for it, at that point there’s no other answer but yes.

Kazan: First of all, was it the Austen you liked the most?

It has been revealed that alderton: Yes. It was the one that I’ve always loved because of Lizzie Bennet. I’ve always been obsessed with Lizzie Bennet. She was my hook. But how about you two? Did you ever dream of adapting these texts?

Recent findings suggest that frost: I was at a place where I stated, “I want to do anything except period, because I’ve done so much period.” Netflix asked me to do The Age of Innocence, and it was, I think at that moment, the one book that made me just go, “Oh my God, okay, let me go back and revisit it.” Because I know I love it, but you have to know what the reason is [to adapt it again]. And the thing that totally blew me away on a reread was how relevant and resonant it is. It is about the freedom of the individual versus the conformity of the pack. It has so many themes in it that are really resonant with social media, the bullying of the group.

Alderton [turning to Kazan]: Tackling Cathy, how did you begin? What was your way into that?

Industry observers note that kazan: I think of adaptation as an advanced form of reading. For me, everything I’ve ever written has come from a feeling of “I have to write this specific thing.” When I was 15 and I read the book for the first time, I felt like it literally grabbed me by the throat and wouldn’t let go. And then I just kept coming back to it. And specifically her character, I felt like I had never read anyone like that before or since.

[to Alderton] The BBC’s Pride and Prejudice—is that the one that you—.

Alderton: No, that wasn’t my Pride and Prejudice.

Alderton: Yeah, the Joe Wright one was the one that I was more familiar with. But I’m so interested in what you were saying about getting to know Cathy. I was kind of nervous about doing press for a book that’s so beloved, and I’m finding it’s actually been really easy so far because I just know the people so well. So much of it has been basically like, putting Mr. Darcy and Elizabeth, all the Bennet family and Bingley through therapy. That psychological interrogation of these very well-known characters has been the thing I’ve just really, really enjoyed.

It has been revealed that frost: Have you both had to change points of view from the novel? Do you feel like you’ve had to make a specific choice about who you are foregrounding? I think I know the answer in your case, Zoe.

It has been revealed that kazan: No, I actually don’t. I’m aware that the way that I read a book is different from the way that anyone else reads that book. When I read East of Eden, I feel like I see Steinbeck becoming enthralled by this character, finding her as curious as I do. I think he starts out a real place of judgment and over the course of the book, really moves towards love and understanding.

So you have to honor that to make it satisfying. That’s kind of frustrating when you’re writing a romantic lead for the first three and a half episodes. None of us, least of all the female protagonist, can see who he is, and we misunderstand him. There is no other option I think than staying with Lizzie.

I think in the book—rightly, because she’s writing from Newland’s point of view—both May and Ellen are sort of constructed as his other. One is the thing to be won, and one is effectively the antagonist. It’s so interesting, because it’s a female author—and [Wharton herself], she’s part Newland. That's who she was growing up. And she’s part Ellen, this woman who now lives in Europe, who's become really cosmopolitan, who is even based on her own love triangle.

The impossibility of that love triangle is the thing I want people to feel. It’s not like one of them is wrong. They're all just feeling what they’re feeling.

Alderton: And how do you feel about bringing that latest perspective and analysis to the story? For a book that's so beloved, did you feel excited by that? Or did you feel kind of daunted by it?

Frost: Maybe I should have felt daunted. I didn’t. I think Edith Wharton—it’s so based on her own personal experience of when she was 45, she had this sexual awakening. She was in this really dull marriage. She’d never had an orgasm. When she was 45, she fell in love with this journalist and had this passionate affair.

Frost: She had this big affair, then he ghosted her. But she was trying to make sense of it through this love triangle. When she wrote it, she couldn’t possibly have written herself as a female character in the center of an illicit love triangle because we were still in time of censorship, and she was being published in a very commercial magazine. So she had to make herself the man that has more agency.

Sources indicate that alderton: With any script, you have a relationship with the characters. But with what we are doing, you have this relationship with the writer.

Alderton: I’ll tell you how I felt about it. I’ve written two novels, both of which I’ve tried to adapt. I found it really, really hard. I found adapting Pride and Prejudice incredibly effortless. When I went from Pride and Prejudice to my novel, I was like, "Why is this so much harder? I hate this novelist. Jane Austen is so much easier.".

What amazed me is just, it’s like she wrote it to be adapted. It’s like her agent had stated to her, “I know you’re going to write this novel about this family of five women, but remember, we could get a great movie deal off the back of it. So try and make it as adaptable as possible.” It has literally been written for TV in this totally perfect six-part structure. I just wish she was around to have written screenplays.

Recent findings suggest that kazan: This is how I feel about Tolstoy too. When I read War and Peace, I’m like, “Oh, he’s seeing it as if it’s a movie.” It’s very strange to read that so far ahead of the technology to make that possible.

Where was each of your point of entry? What was the first scene that you wrote?

It has been revealed that frost: I always break the whole thing in quite a lot of detail to feel like I understand where the story's going. I think when I actually started writing, I probably wrote from the beginning.

Kazan: So you outlined her therapy?

In a recent development, alderton: I do the same. It’s the only thing that gives me freedom and confidence to write.

Kazan: And did you know how many episodes you wanted from the start, or did that change?

Frost: At one point it was longer, and at one point it was shorter. It’s eight in the end. What about you?

Kazan: I wanted eight originally, and then for budget and logistical reasons, I had to boil it down to seven quite late in the process. I had been four years into adapting it.

According to recent reports, kazan: Yeah. And we were a month away from production, and I had to restructure everything quite late in the game.

Kazan: Yeah, but you know what? It was actually this enormous gift. I had this writing teacher in college, a poetry teacher who talked a lot about constraints. And I don’t know if you've ever seen the... What’s his name? He’s a nightmare, but forgive me—the guy who directed Melancholia.

Kazan: There’s this beautiful Lars Von Trier film called The Five Obstructions, a documentary. He challenges his filmmaking teacher to remake this perfect short film that he made in the 1960s with five sets of obstructions to help him break open his creative process again. And that, combined with what my poetry teacher was always saying—which is the form gives you freedom.

Kazan: I feel like having to... Every time I’ve received, “Okay, we don’t have the money for X, or we don’t have the location for Y, or you have to boil eight episodes down to seven,” that it made me think again about, okay, what’s key here? Seeing the instruction as a gift rather than as an obstacle really just helped me over and over again. I actually gave myself one night to be really mad about it, and then the next day I was—.

Kazan: A lot of showrunning, for me at least, has been about learning how to manage my emotions on my own time so that I can go to work and help manage everything. The next day, as soon as I started reworking it, I discovered all of the gifts that it would give me.

Alderton: That lesson is one that you only learn with the privilege of experience. This is only my second TV show. My first, Everything I Know About Love, was an adaptation of my memoir. But I remember now the moments where I said, “If we have to lose this scene, there’s no point shooting the whole show.” Things like that.

Kazan: And then you’re in the edit and you’re like, “Actually, that’s better.”.

In a recent development, alderton: Totally. Or I think back on these things that we couldn’t afford or practically couldn’t work that I really thought would rip out the heart and soul of the show. And now I never dream of an alternate version of that show where those things were put in.

I don’t think I would’ve been as zen as you. I think I would’ve been a petty, grouchy bitch for three days, rather than one.

According to recent reports, kazan: At that point, I was still trying to get my greenlight. I want to hear Dolly’s answer to the first scene question.

According to recent reports, so Elizabeth is walking around Netherfield Park being kind of nosy and breaking the rules, and she’s intrigued by this man. So to give her that line, it felt like we were just off to the races. This is a woman whose preoccupation in life is making sure her daughters are safe. Kazan: Or maybe that’s not a concern.

In a recent development, but it’s interesting that you were saying that thing about chemistry. Kazan: You fall in love, and then sometimes your love affair doesn’t work out.

Industry observers note that alderton: I think there are so many different ways that you can look at diversity with period work. Bridgerton’s a great example of a specific thing. Chapter 2 of GTA 6 begins with Jason and Lucia in a rough spot, with the former still recovering from major injuries sustained at the end of Chapter 1, and the latter having to care for him. Rockstar has yet to officially announce a PC port of GTA 6, but rumors suggest it could be out in early 2027. This would be a very short gap between console and PC releases for a Rockstar-developed game, as the studio's console-first projects usually spend many months in incubation before heading to PC. The threat of a homebrewed PC port, however, could pressure the developer to release GTA 6 on PC sooner rather than later.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, GTA 6 has done phenomenally well on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S since it rolled out last week. The game kicked off with 32.5 million copies sold on its first day, and just a few days later, that number reportedly rose to 44.9 million. PS5 sales have dominated, and Sony claims GTA 6 was the biggest launch in PlayStation history.

Grand Theft Auto 6 gets downright weird when you go off the beaten track, and one secret mission will see you travel to the bowels of hell to fight Beezleboss himself, Satan. This detour is worth it because you'll get cool cosmetics and a powerful shotgun, plus a nice little bump to your health. Here's how you can start this Doom-inspired mission in GTA 6. How to go to Hell in GTA 6 You can find this mission in Port Gellhorn, Kelly County, and it's generally recommended that you tackle it once you've gotten your bearings in Chapter 2 of GTA 6. You can access it with either Jason or Lucia, and you'll need to follow these steps to find it: Start the mission at night, preferably around midnight. Go to the northern section of Port Gellhorn (as indicated on the maps) and look for the Circles of Hell, a house with an open garage. Inside the garage, you'll find two NPCs rocking out. Press L2 to highlight them and start talking. Select the dialogue options "Having fun?" and "It's good" when prompted. Follow the NPCs into a van that appears shortly afterward, and get inside. After being transported to the camping grounds, press L2 to stare into the campfire. Once you've done all that, you'll be taken to Hell, and you'll have to face off against an army of demons. Don't worry! You'll be equipped with a powerful shotgun, so you can mow down the demons and fight your way to Satan. The Prince of Darkness will occasionally summon reinforcements to defend him, but the denizens of hell are no match for a few well-placed shotgun rounds. Finish off the devils, and you'll wake up at the campsite. For your efforts, you'll be rewarded with the following items and upgrades: Circles of Hell top Newly introduced tattoo design Hellspawn Comshot 12 shotgun (collect it next to the throne) Permanent health boost For a closer look at GTA 6's supernatural side, check out how to encounter an unkillable NPC, solve the Bigfoot mystery, and help out some friendly aliens. In 2024, The Brat released a song about her insecurities around the world’s biggest pop star: “I couldn’t even be her if I tried,” she sings. “I’m opposite, I’m on the other side.”.

According to recent reports, in 2025, The Star seemed to clap back to The Brat by releasing a song of her own about their relationship. In it, she accused The Brat of consuming illegal substances—which is fair enough.

In the time since The Brat released a song about The Star, The Exec notes, The Star has “done this performance that she’s supportive of her...but she’s not.” In fact, says The Exec, artists who seem earmarked as The Star’s intentionally DO not collaborate professionally with her rivals, who also seem to be barred from taking part in her social world.

In 2023, The Protégé released a song that appeared to intimate a falling-out between her and a once-beloved mentor: “Trust that you betrayed, confusion that still lingers / Took everything I loved and crushed it in between your fingers.” But then, at the 2024 Grammys, The Star was seen vibing to The Protégé’s performance.

Before that was The California Girl—an adult pretending to be a child—and her feud with The Star, who might be a child pretending to be an adult. And, of course, the Kardashian affair, the details of which we are excluding from this narrative. (Yet another protégé, let’s call her The Blonde, remains in The Star’s good graces.).

“It’s truly Regina George,” The Exec notes.

There once lived a music critic who dared pan The Star. Around then, members of her friend group, one of whom she lived with, were getting courted by The Star. The Critic felt The Star was “ordering friends from a catalog.” After her negative review ran, The Critic’s friends—professional musicians all, who previously credited The Critic for their early success—shunned her. Her roommate, seemingly of her own accord, asked her to move out of their shared duplex. The Star had won.

A SIDE In a 2020 documentary about herself, The Star repeated a story she has often told about how a significant part of her feels frozen at 16, when she became famous. Though if she is frozen at 16, she has repeatedly—and mightily—fought against stasis. In her younger years, she avoided electoral politics, could not see how articulating her opinion was necessary. Later, she found her voice, making statements and endorsements for Democratic candidates, including Kamala Harris for president. She speaks in favor of LGBTQ+ rights, gun control, and making Juneteenth a national holiday. She becomes someone on whom nothing is lost.

B SIDE You only become famous if you really, really want to. Lana Del Rey remarked as much to the BBC in 2024. And The Star really, really did. “She wants it,” Del Rey said. “She’s told me so many times she wants it more than anyone.”.

In a recent development, but if fame is a fickle food, as ­Emily Dickinson—The Star’s sixth cousin, according to Ancestry.com—observed, it is also impunity. You might end up like Barbra Streisand, cloning Coton de Tulears and building a mall in your basement. Or like Jim Carrey, watching YouTube videos all day from your estate in Maui. Or like whatever Elon Musk is doing right now.

Sources indicate that fame also fractures trust. A life grows and shrinks in inverse proportion to the size of its celebrity.

When they were close, The Person Familiar indicates, The Star’s professional life was run by a cabinet of three, including her mother, who acts as The Star’s manager; her longtime tour manager; and her publicist, to whom we only beg for mercy.

Recent findings suggest that “Nobody is beyond reproach with her,” says The Person Familiar. Perhaps not even The Star’s sometimes close and dear friend who, after their private correspondence spilled across the tabloids as part of a public lawsuit, was not seen at The Star’s wedding. “If you don’t see it her way, she comes after you.”.

It has been revealed that “It’s always the same,” The Person Familiar says. “They say something she doesn’t like and they are dead to her. She’d be at dinner at [redacted]’s, then three weeks later, ‘Oh no, I hate her guts.’ ”.

Industry observers note that A/B SIDE Okay, so The Star has a reputation for being punitive. She seems too invested in her own victimhood. Where might she have learned to be so?

Stars function, as cultural theorist Stuart Hall observed, as a mirror. “I want you to know / I’m a mirrorball,” The Star sang in a 2020 hit. “I’ll show you every version of yourself tonight.”.

It has been revealed that the Star holds up a mirror to us, and what the mirror claims is this: If churches were once our society’s primary source of community, identity, and meaning, in these secular times we turn instead to celebrities. And we look, especially, to singers, because who among us is immune to music? The way a song can pitch you forward in space, sustain you through time; the way you swear some songs are written just for you.

A SIDE Stars, they’re just like us. Despite her life in perfect meter, lasting love had long eluded The Star. But it turned out she was a princess, this was a fairy tale, and we were in Hollywood. Her latest beau—regretfully we must call him Redwood—brought to her life a latest form of intensity, a golden light, as they courted at a stadium show, a podcast interview, more indicates, in Instagram posts. They have so much in common, The Star points out: They both perform at stadiums. He practices; she rehearses. He plays games, she plays shows.

And all she had ever wanted from the world was that it celebrate her milky goodness, that her altruism not be mistaken for covert narcissism. Ahead of her wedding, the happy couple donates $26 million to local charities. Since then, The Star released four new songs, rolled out an Oscar campaign, including performing at the Academy Museum Gala, and got a haircut.

In a recent development, B SIDE Summer 2026. The world’s most famous sexy baby—who insists that she is really a monster on a hill—chooses, as the site of her nuptials, midtown Manhattan during a heat wave. Her guests nibble on buffet food as thousands of Newly introduced Yorkers lose power.

In a recent development, it is not lost on them that her $26 million giveaway, apart from being a tax write-off, is akin to a person making $81,228—the median household income in Upcoming York City—giving away $1,055. (In fall 2025, when this article was commissioned, The Star was worth $1.6 billion. By the time this concern goes to press, she will be worth over $2 billion, or the GDP of Eritrea.).

“To become a billionaire,” The Star’s ex Matt Healy once told the Doomscroll podcast, “you don’t really care that much about culture.” He wasn’t speaking specifically about The Star but the deadening effects of modern wealth. Beyond need lies want. Beyond want, greed.

According to recent reports, A/B SIDE And beyond greed was a tricked-out walled garden for the enchanted, her betrothed, and 1,000 of their family and friends, including, according to news reports, at least one government contractor who did not respond to multiple requests for comment. (In March his organization took over our nation’s largest ICE detention facility. Earlier this year a father of three was pronounced dead there, after struggling with five guards, the second death at the camp in as many months. His name was Geraldo Lunas Campos.).

Recent findings suggest that in other news, the wedding reportedly featured a raffle where a lucky guest won a Chanel bag. Another allegedly won a 1970 Chevrolet Chevelle. Madison Square Garden Entertainment Corp. reportedly locked out its own security staff for the occasion, like it was a Mob bar—the kind with no windows. Not even members of the Fresh York Police Department were allowed their own phones on site.

Love may be free, but the performance of it is not. It requires crates, trucks, officers on overtime, private jets, SUVs, HVACs, all the queen’s horses, all the queen’s men, a Jumbotron. Conspiracy theories do not tell you the truth, but they do tell a kind of psychological truth about a place or its people. Had The Star and Redwood filmed the ceremony, perhaps for theatrical release or streaming—maybe on Disney+, which paid The Star a king’s ransom for the rights to another project? (A person with knowledge claims the couple has no prepares to drop a documentary about their big day.).

Recent findings suggest that around the barricades of Madison Square Garden, in the wake left by The Star, her groom, and their guests, her fans gathered. Some had been there for hours, wanting to be nearer to their pious majesty. A white truck passed. Pastries—from the merrymaking gentry presumably, though who can say for certain—were distributed, with an assist from a cop in uniform and gear.

If you listened carefully then to the sounds of the city—not for any semantic meaning, but if you were to really pitch your ears to the utopic promise of music—you might have heard the determined whoosh of a weighted blade dropping, dropping, dropping, the ax of public opinion falling in downward demotic motion.

(The Star’s version was used in the making of this article.).

How To Play GTA 6 On Your PC Or Phone Via Remote Play On Xbox

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (977 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 can be streamed via Xbox Cloud Gaming, and Microsoft has also now confirmed support for Remote Play on Xbox.
  • Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 can be streamed via Xbox Cloud Gaming, and Microsoft has also now confirmed support for Remote Play on Xbox.
  • Remote Play is an Xbox service that lets you stream games from your Xbox Series X|S to a device you might already have, and it's easy to get working.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 can be streamed via Xbox Cloud Gaming, and Microsoft has also now confirmed support for Remote Play on Xbox. This means you can play GTA 6 on your PC, smartphone, or a device like Xbox Rog Ally. Remote Play is an Xbox service that lets you stream games from your Xbox Series X|S to a device you might already have, and it's easy to get working. From your console, select Settings then Devices & connections then Remote features. From there, check the box for Enable remote features. Xbox Remote Play also has a "test" feature so you can preview the experience in your home environment before going further. From there, you can play GTA 6 from a mobile device by accessing the Xbox Remote Play website, selecting the console you want to connect to, and then the device. To play GTA 6 on your PC or Xbox Rog Ally, people can open the Xbox app for PC, click on their profile, then select Accessories & Remote Play and then select Remote Play to choose the device to play on. Additionally, people have spotted that GTA 6's store page on the PlayStation Store now mentions that Remote Play is supported and that PlayStation 5 and PlayStation Portal owners can use cloud streaming if they have a Premium membership. Right now, you need a PS5 or Xbox Series X|S to stream GTA 6, but some are dreaming of the day when you can simply stream the game to your PC or phone without any expensive hardware. That day may eventually come for GTA 6, as Take-Two's own CEO has said the rising cost of gaming hardware is not a good thing and that streaming games could be a massive business very soon. “If you believe in streaming, and to be clear, we really do, and I’m happy to put a timeline on it. I think we’ll be in commercial streaming mode within three years, and by commercial, I mean low latency," Strauss Zelnick said. "That can 10x the effective installed base. Now, it doesn’t mean we’re going to 10x our revenue–and we wouldn’t project that we would–but because obviously your avid consumers already had access to video game machines. But I do think it creates great opportunity for titles that are broadly desirable, even outside of core markets.” GTA 6 is doing just fine without the potential expanded reach of streaming. After all, the game sold 32.5 million copies before launch and generated close to $4 billion in revenue by day one. Even if GTA 6 doesn't add support for full streaming without a console, the game is expected to expand its reach in a major way in 2027 with an expected PC release. Beyond that, GTA 6 is reportedly going to add an online mode in 2027 as well, and it could be bigger than Fortnite.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, next month marks the second anniversary of Marvel Rivals, and to celebrate, a new Lego set is on the way that lets you build the game's unofficial mascot, Jeff the Land Shark.
  • The 495-piece set captures the adorable strategist in all his glory, including his big eyes, toothy smile, huge tongue, and even his collar.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that next month marks the second anniversary of Marvel Rivals, and to celebrate, a newly introduced Lego set is on the way that lets you build the game's unofficial mascot, Jeff the Land Shark. While we regularly see Lego Marvel sets roll out, this is the first-ever Marvel Rivals kit, and it'll go on sale starting January 1, 2027, priced at $50. GameSpot can also exclusively reveal the first images of Jeff below, showing the completed build alongside his box art. See at The Lego Store The 495-piece set captures the adorable strategist in all his glory, including his substantial eyes, toothy smile, huge tongue, and even his collar. This won't be a static figure either: once fully assembled, Jeff has a movable head, legs, tail, and fins that let builders recreate his joyful trot, swimming, and battle poses. For added touches, his collar includes his signature name tag, his tongue can be removed to close his mouth, and his fin can be detached so builders can replicate Jeff's Hide-and-Seek movement ability from the game. "Jeff brings together everything players love about a breakout gaming character: an unforgettable silhouette, a personality you understand instantly, and the ability to turn any match into a story," Lego Marvel design lead Jesper C. Nielsen mentioned in a press release. "We wanted this Lego model to capture both sides of him, from the lovable companion fans want beside their screen to the unpredictable strategist they meet in battle." Meanwhile, Jeff and the rest of the Marvel Rivals roster are preparing to cap off an entire year of Avengers-centric events that have been building up to the game's big Avengers: Doomsday tie-in. Season 11.5 kicks off on December 11. Nightcrawler was recently added to the game, bringing mutant energy, swords, and teleportation strategies, and he'll soon be followed by Marvel's unique take on Dracula, who has spent the last few months hibernating and healing for the battles ahead.

Video doorbells from Ring, Blink, Arlo, Google, and several other brands are discounted in Amazon's Black Friday 2026 sale, with prices starting at just $28 for the Arlo Wireless Video Doorbell 2K and savings reaching $100 on the Ring Wired Doorbell 4K Pro. The deals cover everything from affordable battery-powered models that are easy to install to higher-resolution options that can capture more detail around your doorstep, so there's something for different budgets and home security needs. For more such editor-vetted deals, check out our Black Friday coverage.

It has been revealed that the Ring Battery Doorbell 2K is down to $39.99 from $99.99, saving you $60. It records in 2K resolution with a head-to-toe view, so you can see who's at your door and check for packages left on the doorstep. You also get motion alerts and two-way audio through the Ring app, while its rechargeable battery makes installation relatively straightforward without having to deal with doorbell wiring.

For a more advanced option, the Ring Battery Doorbell 2K Plus is down to $89.99 from $179.99, saving you $90. It builds on the standard model with enhanced video processing and additional detection capabilities, while retaining the convenience of battery-powered installation, two-way communication, and motion alerts. You can read more about its features and performance in PCMag's review.

The Ring Wired Doorbell 4K Pro is down to $149.99 from $249.99, saving you $100 on Ring's premium wired doorbell. It records in sharper 4K resolution, making it easier to pick out details around your front entrance, and supports advanced motion detection and two-way audio—and since it connects to existing doorbell wiring, you also won't have to worry about recharging a battery. For more on it, check out PCMag's review.

In a recent development, amazon's other doorbell brand, Blink, has the Blink Battery Doorbell 2K+ down to $34.99 from $79.99. For that price, you get a 2K camera with a wider view of your doorstep, along with Alexa compatibility and motion alerts sent directly to your phone. For a closer look at how it performs, check out PCMag’s review.

For an even cheaper battery-powered option, the Arlo Wireless Video Doorbell 2K HDR (2nd Gen) is down to $28 from $79.99, making it the most affordable model in this roundup. Despite its lower price, it records in 2K HDR and has a 180-degree diagonal field of view and up to 12x digital zoom. For more on it, check out PCMag's review.

It has been revealed that another affordable battery-powered option is the Tapo 2K Wireless Smart Video Doorbell (D205), now $37.98 from $49.99. Along with 2K video and a wide field of view to help you keep an eye on visitors and deliveries, it supports local recording to a compatible microSD card (sold separately), so you can save footage without paying for cloud storage.

The Wyze Battery Video Doorbell HD+ is another option worth considering at $49.98, down from $65.98. It runs for three to six months on its built-in battery (or can be hardwired for continuous power) and records at 1536 x 1536 resolution with a square field of view that captures visitors from head to toe. It's also IP65-rated for weather resistance.

Industry observers note that the Eufy Security Video Doorbell E340, now $99.99 from $169.99, has a dual-camera setup—one records visitors in 2K, while the other points down at your doorstep to monitor delivered packages. It also offers color night vision, a removable rechargeable battery, and 8GB of built-in storage, so you can save and review recordings without paying for a cloud subscription. For more on its features and performance, check out PCMag's review.

In a recent development, for anyone already using myQ-compatible garage door products, Chamberlain's myQ 2K Video Doorbell could be a convenient addition, especially now that it's down to $37.98 from $99.99. It offers 2K video, motion alerts, and two-way audio to help you keep track of visitors and deliveries.

The Google Nest Doorbell (Battery) is $154.99, down from $199.99, and offers HDR video, intelligent alerts for people, animals, vehicles, and packages, and battery-powered installation. You can read PCMag's review of the Nest Doorbell for more details.

For those with existing doorbell wiring, the newer third-generation Google Nest Doorbell is also on sale for $179.99 (was $199.99), offering sharper 2K video and continuous power without the need for recharging. For more on it, check out PCMag’s review.
